Pulay (1969), PySCF developers (2026), DFTK developers (2026) Finite-difference checks: smaller displacements are not always better One Cartesian component of one atom is displaced by ±h from the baseline configuration. At each displaced geometry the SCF is converged independently, and the resulting total energies give a central-difference force. The lattice, k points and weights, basis name, FFT grid, functional, pseudopotential and electron count are aligned. The atom-centered basis moves too, so this probes derivatives of the same discrete energy including basis-position dependence. For a smooth energy surface, central-difference truncation is O(h²). SCF solution and roundoff errors in energies are divided by 2h, so very small displacements can increase errors. Several h values are retained to locate a stable agreement range with analytic forces. A clean U-shaped measured curve is not assumed. An input SCF energy tolerance is not interpreted as a rigorous bound on the error of each energy. Agreement with finite differences from the same engine checks internal consistency, including signs, components and basis derivatives. Both use shared functional and pseudopotential implementations, so this alone is not an independent physical reference. A separate plane-wave DFTK implementation provides the independent comparison here. FIαFD(h)=−E(R+heIα)−E(R−heIα)2h FFD(h)−F=O(h2)+O(δE/h) Sources: P. Pulay (1969), PySCF developers (2026) Converge basis, k points, auxiliary grids and SCF for forces separately A small energy change alone does not establish converged forces. The Gaussian orbital basis, Brillouin-zone mesh, auxiliary FFT grid and SCF stopping conditions are varied one at a time, comparing forces on the same atoms and Cartesian components. Atom ordering and axes are fixed. Summaries use an L∞-type maximum absolute component norm, distinct from a per-atom vector magnitude or a component average. Increasing a basis’s zeta label does not necessarily produce nested spaces or monotonic force changes. Nor are all k meshes nested. The final pair of settings is compared with a published target, without presenting the increment as a rigorous complete-basis or infinite-k-point error bound. The auxiliary FFT representation of density and local potentials is a separate convergence axis from the Gaussian orbital space. Incomplete SCF convergence also affects forces. Alongside termination flags and iteration counts, inspect stored electron-count, orbital and SCF residual diagnostics. Force sensitivity to tighter stopping conditions is measured directly, and an unconverged electronic state must not be returned to BOMD as an accepted force. Each sweep varies one control while holding the other controls at the finite settings specified in the public input. Basis sequences are checked separately at Γ and 2³, but no joint calculation combines 4³ sampling, the largest Gaussian basis and the finest FFT grid. Independent-reference agreement applies only to the designated Γ and 2³ cases. ∥ΔF∥∞=max⁡I,α∈{x,y,z}∣FIα(a)−FIα(b)∣ ΔbasisF,ΔkF,ΔFFTF,Fτ−Ftight Sources: PySCF developers (2026), DFTK developers (2026), J. M. Herbert and M. Head-Gordon (2005) Independent reference: the same model in a different discretization PySCF uses a periodic Gaussian basis and FFTDF; the reference uses DFTK’s plane-wave Hamiltonian, SCF, periodic ion interactions and analytic forces. Lattice and all atomic positions, valence count, spin restriction and integer occupations, every local-GTH coefficient, Libxc LDA_X plus LDA_C_VWN (VWN5), fractional k points and weights are matched. No fitted energy offset or force correction is applied. The DFTK plane-wave cutoff is increased separately and its final force increment is measured. This is not a rounding-error comparison of identical finite matrices. Different finite Gaussian and plane-wave spaces are assessed using the published acceptance width and convergence diagnostics on both sides. Both engines share Libxc, which limits the extent of implementation independence. DFTK compute_forces returns a representation associated with fractional coordinates; the Cartesian API is compute_forces_cart. Coordinate and force transformations are different. Comparisons here use Cartesian components in hartree/bohr throughout. The generation script, pinned Julia environment, pseudopotential, input and result hashes are retained. Comparing against the saved reference in Python and regenerating the reference in Julia are distinct operations. R=Aξ,Fcart=−A−T∇ξE Sources: S. Goedecker, M. Teter and J. Hutter (1996), S. H. Vosko, L. Wilk and M. Nusair (1980), Qiming Sun et al. (2020), M. F. Herbst, A. Levitt and E. Cancès (2021), DFTK developers (2026) Check components, translation and nonzero forces A configuration with nearly zero forces can pass even with a sign error. A multiatom configuration carrying nonzero forces is used, with componentwise comparisons of analytic forces, finite differences and the independent reference. A single force norm should not hide component permutations, atom-order mistakes or incorrect units. In an ideal periodic system without external fields, uniform translation leaves the total energy unchanged and the sum of atomic forces vanishes. Finite real-space grids can numerically break this property; the remaining total force is a useful grid and differentiation diagnostic. Translation checks alone do not establish accurate relative forces, so energy differences and an independent reference are used alongside them. E({RI+t})=E({RI})⟹∑IFI=0 Sources: DFTK developers (2026), PySCF developers (2026) The BOMD interface and additional trajectory validation The BOMD force provider energy_and_forces accepts positions_bohr and returns energy_per_cell and forces_cartesian from the same energy surface, together with SCF convergence and residual diagnostics. An unconverged electronic state is treated as a failure. Masses belong to nuclear time integration, not as factors multiplying the DFT potential energy or forces. Wrapped positions inside a periodic cell must be distinguished from a continuous trajectory record. Velocity Verlet advances velocities by half a step, updates positions, solves the electronic problem again for the new forces, then completes the velocity update. Carrying an electronic guess from a previous step accelerates the calculation but does not replace SCF convergence. This verification focuses on atomic forces and the BOMD handoff; a single force evaluation or short interface smoke test is not counted as validation of long trajectories. Accepting a practical trajectory additionally requires timestep refinement, tighter-SCF comparisons, total-energy and momentum checks in unthermostatted NVE, and time-reversal checks where appropriate. Thermostats can hide force or integration errors by absorbing energy changes, so unthermostatted checks come first. Small short-time drift does not guarantee long-time stability or a correct statistical distribution. Car–Parrinello dynamics is a distinct formulation propagating fictitious electronic degrees of freedom alongside nuclei. A force provider on the Born–Oppenheimer surface is not a CPMD implementation. text.ja: Particle-in-Cell（PIC） プラズマPICは速度分布を代表粒子で、自己無撞着な場を格子で表現します。粒子同士のCoulomb力をすべて直接足す方法とは、平滑化・衝突性・統計誤差が異なります。 対象と代表式 まず非相対論的・静電的なVlasov–Poisson系を考えます。代表粒子pの重みwₚ、電荷qₚ、位置xₚから格子電荷ρᵢを作ります。Sᵢは粒子形状から得る無次元割当係数でΣᵢSᵢ=1、Vᵢはセル体積です。E=−∇φとし、Poisson方程式を同じ境界条件で解きます。 ρi=1Vi∑pwpqpSi(xp),−∇h2ϕi=ρi/ϵ0,v˙p=(qp/mp)Eh(xp). 計算の流れ 電荷の割当、Poisson解法、電場の粒子位置への補間、粒子の押し出しを繰り返します。背景イオンもρに含めます。電磁PICへ進む場合は電流割当とMaxwell更新を加え、離散連続の式との整合を確認します。Dawsonのシート模型は歴史的な粒子プラズマの例であり、全PIC方式の定義ではありません。 適用条件と落とし穴 陽的静電PICではプラズマ振動の時間尺度とDebye長の解像を調べます。必要条件は押し出し法・形状・場の解法で変わり、万能なΔtやセル幅はありません。粒子数を増やす統計収束と格子/時間刻みの収束を分け、自己力・有限格子加熱にも注意します。 追加版は静止した一様イオン背景を持つ1次元周期・静電cold-electron PICです。CIC割当・補間、Poisson場と粒子押し出しの固定例であり、熱的Landau減衰、電磁PIC、イオン運動は対象外です。 検証するときに見る量 単一粒子の自己力、中性一様分布、微小振幅のプラズマ振動やLandau減衰から始めます。総電荷、エネルギードリフト、粒子数依存と独立乱数系列を報告します。減衰率は理論の線形振幅域に限って比較します。 線形の冷たいプラズマ振動を小振幅の参照とし、格子・時間刻み・粒子数を分けて比較します。総電荷、場の残差、自己力、粒子運動量と粒子・場エネルギーの診断を別々に示します。保存診断の小ささだけで軌道精度や任意の長時間安定性を保証しません。 追加版では固定CIC空間系の運動をDOP853でも積分し、公差と最大刻みの感度を調べます。これは時間積分の別アルゴリズムによる照合であり、独立した連続Vlasov–Poissonソルバーではありません。粒子数の乱数検査は初期時刻の単一Fourier電荷モードのpowerが対象で、CICの有限格子応答を含めて解析期待値と比較します。粒子数増大による任意の非線形軌道の収束とは区別します。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 CIC静電PICの冷たいプラズマ振動 固定した標的の計算例 1次元周期セルの電子をCICで格子と結び、Poisson方程式と粒子運動を自洽に進めます。 有限振幅・有限粒子数の誤差床があります。非線形不安定性、Landau減衰、衝突、電磁PIC、相対論粒子、境界流入出の検証ではありません。 入力・結果・受入条件 · 手法・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：electrostatics.py · コード：fmm.py · コード：transport.py · テスト：test_particles.py · 配布ZIP · 保存結果 text.en: Particle-in-cell / PIC Plasma PIC represents a distribution by computational particles and self-consistent fields by a mesh. Its smoothing, collisionality and sampling error differ from direct all-pairs Coulomb dynamics. Problem and representative equations Start with nonrelativistic electrostatic Vlasov–Poisson. Computational particle p has weight wₚ, charge qₚ and position xₚ. Dimensionless shape weights Sᵢ sum to one, and Vᵢ is cell volume. Deposit ρ, solve Poisson with the stated boundary conditions, and use E=−∇φ. ρi=1Vi∑pwpqpSi(xp),−∇h2ϕi=ρi/ϵ0,v˙p=(qp/mp)Eh(xp). Algorithm Repeat charge deposition, field solution, particle gathering and particle pushing; include background ions in ρ. Electromagnetic PIC additionally needs current deposition and Maxwell updates consistent with discrete continuity. Dawson’s sheet model is a historical particle-plasma example, not the definition of every PIC discretization. Conditions and pitfalls Explicit electrostatic PIC must examine plasma-frequency time scales and Debye-length resolution. Exact restrictions depend on the particle pusher, shape and field solver. Separate sampling convergence in particle count from grid/time convergence, and check self-force and finite-grid heating. The companion is one-dimensional periodic electrostatic cold-electron PIC with a fixed uniform ion background. It is a fixed CIC deposit/gather, Poisson-field and particle-push example; thermal Landau damping, electromagnetic PIC and moving ions are outside its scope. What to check Begin with single-particle self-force, a uniform neutral distribution, and small-amplitude plasma oscillations or Landau damping. Report charge, energy drift, particle-count dependence and independent random realizations. Compare damping rates only within the linear-amplitude regime used by the theory. Use linear cold-plasma oscillation as a small-amplitude reference and vary mesh, time step and particle count separately. Report charge, field residual, self-force, particle momentum and particle-plus-field energy diagnostics separately. Small conservation diagnostics alone guarantee neither trajectory accuracy nor arbitrary long-time stability. The companion also integrates the fixed CIC spatial system with DOP853 and tests tolerance/maximum-step sensitivity. This is an alternative time-integration algorithm, not an independent continuum Vlasov–Poisson solver. The random particle-count check concerns the initial power of one Fourier charge mode, compared with its analytic expectation including the finite-grid CIC response. It is distinct from particle-count convergence of arbitrary nonlinear trajectories. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Cold-plasma oscillation with electrostatic CIC PIC Computation for a fixed target Couple electrons to a 1D periodic grid by CIC, solving Poisson and particle motion self-consistently. Finite amplitude and finite particles leave an error floor. Nonlinear instabilities, Landau damping, collisions, electromagnetic/relativistic PIC and open particle boundaries are unvalidated. DOP853 is not an independent PIC spatial implementation. Distinguish charge/momentum preservation from approximate energy conservation. Initial-noise N scaling does not validate evolved warm plasmas. Landau damping, electromagnetic/relativistic PIC and collisions remain unvalidated. text.ja: PINN・ニューラル演算子 PINNは特定の問題の近似解をニューラル関数として学習し、neural operatorは係数場や初期条件から解の関数への写像を学びます。同じニューラルネットでも、学習対象と検証方法が違います。 対象と代表式 PINNではu_θのPDE残差、境界残差、データ残差を重みλで足した経験損失を最小化します。NとBはPDE・境界演算子、f,gは与えた右辺です。FNOはvを特徴関数とし、Fourier空間の積分核Kと局所作用Wを組み合わせる層の代表形を使います。 L(θ)=λr⟨∣N[uθ]−f∣2⟩r+λb⟨∣B[uθ]−g∣2⟩b+λd⟨∣uθ−uobs∣2⟩d. vℓ+1=σ ⁣(Wℓvℓ+F−1[Kℓ Fvℓ]). 計算の流れ PINNでは領域と単位をスケーリングし、自動微分で残差を作り、学習点と境界条件の課し方を指定して最適化します。FNOでは入力・参照解の集合で写像を学習し、Fourierモードを有限数に切ります。原PINN論文とFNO論文は別の提案です。 適用条件と落とし穴 小さい訓練損失は、領域全体の小さい解誤差や保存則の保証ではありません。残差項の不均衡、衝撃波、硬い尺度、学習分布外の入力を調べます。格子間転送の可能性と、任意解像度で正しい物理を再現する保証も区別します。 検証するときに見る量 解析解または独立に収束させた従来法と比較し、学習点外のL1/L2/L∞誤差、境界・保存則、複数seedを測ります。operator学習では同じ軌道の近接時刻を無作為分割するだけでなく、問題単位でtrain/testを分け、入力分布外も別報告します。 公開範囲と関連項目 解説・代表式・文献を公開しています。専用コードと数値検証結果は実装予定です。上記の検証案は未実施で、他の手法のコードや計算結果をこの手法の検証として流用しません。 PINN・ニューラル演算子 一次文献・関連資料と確認範囲 原著、後続の変種、著者による著書、概説、公式資料を区別して参照します。DOI・書誌の確認と原文の該当箇所の閲覧を区別し、論文全体の監査や数値再現を行ったという意味ではありません。確認範囲の注記は引用ごとに示します。 M. text.en: PINNs and neural operators A PINN fits a neural representation of a particular solution; a neural operator learns a map from input functions such as coefficients or initial data to solution functions. Their targets and validation protocols differ. Problem and representative equations A PINN minimizes an empirical weighted loss of PDE, boundary and data residuals. N and B are differential/boundary operators and f,g are prescribed data. A representative FNO layer combines a Fourier-parameterized integral operator K with a local map W acting on feature functions v. L(θ)=λr⟨∣N[uθ]−f∣2⟩r+λb⟨∣B[uθ]−g∣2⟩b+λd⟨∣uθ−uobs∣2⟩d. vℓ+1=σ ⁣(Wℓvℓ+F−1[Kℓ Fvℓ]). Algorithm For a PINN, scale coordinates/units, differentiate residuals, specify collocation points and boundary enforcement, and optimize. FNO trains an operator on input/reference-solution pairs and truncates Fourier modes. Cite the PINN and FNO papers as separate proposals. Conditions and pitfalls Small training loss is not a bound on global solution error or conservation. Examine residual imbalance, shocks, stiff scales and out-of-distribution inputs. Transfer between discretizations is not a guarantee of physical correctness at arbitrary resolution. What to check Compare against analytic or independently converged conventional solutions. Measure off-training L1/L2/L∞ errors, boundaries, conservation and multiple seeds. Split operator data by independent problems rather than nearby time slices alone, and report distribution-shift tests separately. Publication scope and related entries Reading, representative equations and sources are published. Dedicated code and numerical verification remain planned. The suggested checks above are not measured results, and code/results of other methods are not presented as validation of this method. text.ja: Particle Mesh Ewald（PME） PMEはEwald法の逆空間項を粒子から格子へ移し、FFTを使う方法です。原PMEのLagrange補間と、後のSPMEのB-spline補間を区別して読みます。 対象と代表式 中性・3次元周期のCoulomb系で、格子点xₘに割り当てた電荷Qₘを考えます。Wₘは割当重み、ĜₕはEwaldのGaussian因子、格子規約、補間補正を含む逆空間作用素です。この模式式は逆空間部分だけで、実空間・自己項を置き換えません。 Qm=∑iqiWm(ri),ϕh=Fh−1 ⁣[G^h FhQ]. 計算の流れ 原法では局所Lagrange補間で電荷を格子へ割り当て、離散Fourier変換、格子上の畳み込み、逆変換を行います。力の微分方法と粒子への補間を一組として定義します。格子上で得た電場とエネルギー微分の力が、選んだ離散化で一致するとは限りません。 適用条件と落とし穴 格子を細かくする誤差、補間次数、Ewaldの打切り、力の微分規約を混ぜずに比較します。FFTの正規化とk=0、単位を明記します。O(N log N)は通常の格子増大の仮定を伴う計算量の説明で、精度の保証ではありません。 ここで結ぶ公開コードの採用形はB-splineの解析的エネルギー勾配を使うsmooth PMEです。1993年のLagrange補間PMEを実装・検証したという意味ではなく、元のPMEの式・文献・適用条件を保って別の採用変種へ案内します。 検証するときに見る量 同一の小さい中性セルについて、十分収束した直接Ewald和を参照にします。格子数・補間次数・分割定数を変え、エネルギーと力のRMS/最大誤差、平行移動依存性を調べます。重力PMの成功をPMEの検証に流用しません。 追加版では同じ中性周期電荷に対し格子数・B-spline order・共通平行移動を変え、収束した直接Ewaldと別実装theta積分に比較します。直接Ewaldとの共有実空間・自己項があるため、その一致だけを独立な全エネルギー検証とはしません。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 text.en: Particle mesh Ewald / PME PME transfers the reciprocal Ewald calculation to a mesh and uses FFTs. Distinguish the original Lagrange-interpolation PME from the later B-spline construction of SPME. Problem and representative equations For a neutral triply periodic Coulomb system, Qₘ is charge assigned to mesh point xₘ using weights Wₘ. The reciprocal operator Ĝₕ includes Ewald screening, mesh conventions and interpolation corrections. This schematic describes only the reciprocal contribution; real-space and self terms remain necessary. Qm=∑iqiWm(ri),ϕh=Fh−1 ⁣[G^h FhQ]. Algorithm Assign charges with local Lagrange polynomials, transform the mesh, apply the reciprocal convolution and transform back. Specify the differentiation and particle-gather rules together. A mesh-interpolated field and the derivative of the discrete energy need not give identical forces. Conditions and pitfalls Separate mesh resolution, interpolation order, Ewald cutoffs and force differentiation in error studies. State FFT normalization, k=0 treatment and units. The usual O(N log N) description assumes an appropriate mesh-growth regime and is not an accuracy guarantee. The linked implementation adopts smooth PME with B-spline analytical energy gradients. It does not implement or validate the original 1993 Lagrange-interpolation PME; the original PME equations, sources and applicability remain distinct from this implemented variant. What to check Use a converged direct Ewald calculation for the identical neutral cell. Vary mesh size, interpolation order and screening; measure RMS/maximum energy and force errors and sensitivity to common translations. A gravity-PM test does not validate PME. The companion varies mesh size, B-spline order and common translation for the same neutral periodic charges, comparing against converged direct Ewald and a separately implemented theta integral. The direct-Ewald comparison shares real-space/self terms, so agreement there alone is not independent validation of the entire energy. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Mesh/order convergence of B-spline smooth PME Computation for a fixed target A small smooth-PME example assigns charge with B-splines and evaluates the Ewald reciprocal contribution by FFT. Finite-mesh aliasing permits nonzero net force for this energy-gradient variant; that diagnostic is reported. No exact momentum conservation, long MD, original PME, optimized P³M or slab validation is claimed. Finite-mesh aliasing generally gives nonzero net force for this energy-gradient variant. No exact momentum conservation, arbitrary-configuration error bound, long MD, original PME or every SPME variant is certified. text.ja: QR・SVD・最小二乗 最小二乗、低ランク近似、条件数の診断には、同じ行列でも異なる分解が役立ちます。QRは直交化と三角系へ、SVDは特異値と可解な方向へ問題を分けます。 対象と代表式 m≥nの実行列Aに対する薄いQRではQᵀQ=I、Rは上三角です。列フルランクなら最小二乗解はRx=Qᵀbで求まります。SVDのσᵢは非負の特異値で、閾値以下を切る疑似逆行列は、元と同じ問題ではなく正則化した問題を解きます。 A=QR=UΣVT,min⁡x∥Ax−b∥2,A+b=∑σi>τuiTbσivi(truncated). 計算の流れ Householder反射で列の下側を消すQRは、通常のGram–Schmidtより直交性を保ちやすい構成です。ランク診断には列ピボットやSVDを検討します。SVDは直交変換で二重対角へ落としてから処理する代表方式があり、正規方程式を明示的に作る必要はありません。 適用条件と落とし穴 2ノルムではκ₂(AᵀA)=κ₂(A)²となり、正規方程式は条件を悪化させます。小さい残差でも、悪条件やノイズがあれば係数は不確かです。ランクの閾値はスケール・丸め・観測誤差に応じて定め、単位の違う列のスケーリングも検討します。 残差・後退誤差と、求めた係数・特異値の前進誤差を区別します。条件数が大きければ、入力や右辺の小さな摂動が係数を大きく変えることがあります。数値階数は特異値の閾値と精度に依存する規約で、階数を切り捨てた最小二乗解は元と同じ問題の厳密解とは限りません。 一般の最小二乗問題では、条件数だけでなく右辺と列空間の角度にも感度が依存します。片側Jacobi SVDの高い相対精度に関する文献上の結果にも、停止規準や成分ごとの条件付けという仮定があります。今回の小行列で微小特異値が一致しても、任意の悪条件行列への万能な相対精度を意味しません。 検証するときに見る量 A−QR、QᵀQ−I、A−UΣVᵀの相対ノルム、最小二乗の正規性Aᵀ(Ax−b)を調べます。特異値が既知の行列とランク欠損例で、入力摂動に対する解の変化も比較します。 追加版では既知の特異値を持つ小行列、右辺の固定摂動、階数判定の閾値を用い、条件数に沿って誤差を比較します。QR・SVDの再構成と直交性、最小二乗残差、係数の前進誤差、数値階数を別々に測ります。LAPACK参照に加え、実際の二進浮動小数点入力を高精度演算に移した独立参照を区別します。正規方程式による条件数の二乗化は上の理論説明であり、この追加例で実行した対照とはしません。 text.en: QR, SVD and least squares Least squares, low-rank approximation and conditioning call for different matrix decompositions. QR reduces a problem to orthogonal transformations and a triangular solve; SVD exposes singular values and resolvable directions. Problem and representative equations For a real m×n matrix with m≥n, thin QR has QᵀQ=I and upper triangular R. Full column rank gives the least-squares solve Rx=Qᵀb. SVD has nonnegative singular values σᵢ. Truncating small σᵢ in a pseudoinverse regularizes the problem and can change the solution being sought. A=QR=UΣVT,min⁡x∥Ax−b∥2,A+b=∑σi>τuiTbσivi(truncated). Algorithm Householder QR eliminates subdiagonal entries with reflections and generally maintains orthogonality better than classical Gram–Schmidt. Consider column pivoting or SVD for rank diagnosis. Classical SVD algorithms reduce to bidiagonal form using orthogonal transformations rather than explicitly forming normal equations. Conditions and pitfalls For full column rank, κ₂(AᵀA)=κ₂(A)². A small residual can coexist with uncertain coefficients under ill-conditioning or noise. Choose a numerical-rank threshold relative to scale, rounding and measurement uncertainty, and consider column scaling when variables have different units. Distinguish residual/backward error from forward errors in coefficients or singular values. At large condition numbers, small changes to the input or right-hand side can cause large coefficient changes. Numerical rank depends on a singular-value threshold and arithmetic precision; a truncated least-squares solution need not solve the original problem exactly. General least-squares sensitivity also depends on the angle between the right-hand side and the column space, not only on condition number. Published relative-accuracy results for one-sided Jacobi SVD depend on stopping rules and componentwise conditioning. Agreement for small singular values in these small matrices is not a universal relative-accuracy guarantee for arbitrary ill-conditioned matrices. What to check Check relative factorization residuals, orthogonality and Aᵀ(Ax−b). Test prescribed singular values and rank-deficient cases, and compare solution changes under controlled data perturbations. The added release compares errors across small matrices with prescribed singular values, fixed right-hand-side perturbations and numerical-rank thresholds. Measure QR/SVD reconstruction and orthogonality, least-squares residual, coefficient forward error and numerical rank separately. Distinguish LAPACK references from independent high-precision references constructed from the actual binary floating-point input. Condition-number squaring for normal equations is explained above as theory; it is not an executed control in this added case. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD: orthogonality, rank and least squares Computation for a fixed target Original Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD for real tall matrices are checked on ordinary, 10⁶-column-scaled and rank-deficient inputs, against separate LAPACK singular values and minimum-norm least-squares solutions. Not a full LAPACK replacement or validation of complex/wide matrices, arbitrary extreme scales or optimal relative singular-value accuracy. The 10⁻¹² cutoff defines numerical rather than exact mathematical rank. The experiment does not establish all hypotheses of the Demmel–Veselić accuracy results. text.ja: Gauss求積・適応積分 Gauss求積は重みに適合する節点と重みを選び、少ない点数で多項式積分を正確にします。適応積分は区間ごとの誤差推定を使って評価点を配分する別の考え方です。 対象と代表式 正の重みw(x)に対するn点Gauss則は、条件が整えば次数2n−1以下の多項式に厳密です。直交多項式の三項漸化係数で作るJacobi行列Jの固有値が節点、正規化固有ベクトルvの第1成分の二乗とμ₀=∫wが求積重みになります。 ∫abf(x)w(x) dx≈∑j=1nωjf(xj),Jvj=xjvj,ωj=μ0(vj)12. 計算の流れ Golub–Welsch法はこの対称三重対角固有値問題を解きます。適応Gauss–Kronrod型では入れ子の2つの則の差を局所誤差の指標にし、区間を分割して絶対/相対許容誤差と照合します。両者の差は厳密な誤差上界とは限りません。 適用条件と落とし穴 点特異性、不連続、高速振動、広い領域の細いピークでは、評価点が構造を見落とします。既知の不連続で区間を分け、必要なら変数変換や重み付き則を使います。積分値が0に近いと相対誤差だけの停止判定は不適切です。 積分が相殺で小さくなるときは、∫|f|/|∫f|のような相殺条件数も有用です。絶対誤差・相対誤差と、積分則内部の誤差推定値は別の量です。有限個の評価点が狭い山をすべて見逃す対照では、二つの近似の差が小さくても真の積分誤差が大きくなり得ます。 条件数を比べるときは入力摂動のノルムと摂動モデルを明示し、積分値が0なら相対条件数・相対誤差を未定義として絶対量で評価します。 検証するときに見る量 単項式の厳密積分で厳密次数を確認し、解析積分できる非多項式、特異点と細いピークでも試します。推定誤差と真の誤差、評価回数、分割上限到達の終了理由を分けて残します。 追加版では求積点数・許容誤差を変え、既知の積分値を持つ滑らかな関数、相殺を伴う関数、固定した狭い山の対照を独立参照と比較します。真の誤差、推定誤差、関数評価回数を分けて記録します。狭い山を明示的に分割して捉える計算と見逃す診断対照を区別し、全ての被積分関数への誤差保証とはしません。 端点で導関数が特異になる例は変数変換の前後を比較し、評価回数や再帰深さの上限への到達も終了状態として残します。 Legendreの3項漸化式からGauss節点と重みを構成し、2n−1次までの多項式モーメントと指数関数を検査します。適応Simpsonは指数関数とLorentz型ピークを積分し、解析積分・独立QUADPACKと比較します。 Simpsonの局所推定は任意の関数に対する厳密な誤差上界ではありません。高周波の見落とし、特異点、丸め誤差の停滞を一般に解決する実装ではなく、Gauss–KronrodやQUADPACK全体の再実装でもありません。 入力・結果・受入条件 · 手法・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：solvers.py · テスト：test_foundations.py · 配布ZIP · text.en: Gaussian and adaptive quadrature Gaussian quadrature selects nodes and weights for a measure to integrate polynomials efficiently. Adaptive integration separately allocates function evaluations using local error estimates. Problem and representative equations For a positive measure, an n-point Gaussian rule is exact through degree 2n−1 when the required moments exist. The Jacobi matrix J of orthogonal-polynomial recurrence coefficients has quadrature nodes as eigenvalues. Weights are μ₀ times squared first components of normalized eigenvectors, with μ₀=∫w. ∫abf(x)w(x) dx≈∑j=1nωjf(xj),Jvj=xjvj,ωj=μ0(vj)12. Algorithm Golub–Welsch solves this symmetric tridiagonal eigenproblem. Adaptive Gauss–Kronrod-type integration uses differences between nested rules to estimate local errors, subdivides intervals and checks absolute/relative tolerances. The rule difference is not an unconditional error bound. Conditions and pitfalls Singularities, jumps, rapid oscillations and narrow peaks can be missed by sampled nodes. Split at known discontinuities and consider transformations or matched weighted rules. Relative tolerance alone is unsuitable when the integral is close to zero. When cancellation makes an integral small, a cancellation condition number such as integral(|f|)/|integral(f)| is informative. Absolute/relative true errors differ from a rule’s internal error estimate. If finitely many sample points miss a narrow bump, agreement between two approximations can coexist with a large true integration error. State the input-perturbation norm and perturbation model when comparing condition numbers; if the integral is zero, relative condition and relative error are undefined, so report absolute quantities. What to check Verify degree of exactness on monomials, then test nonpolynomials with known integrals, singularities and narrow peaks. Record estimated versus true error, evaluation count and termination caused by subdivision limits. The added release varies rule order and tolerance for smooth functions with known integrals, cancellation-sensitive functions and a fixed narrow-bump control. Compare against independent references and record true error, estimated error and function evaluations separately. Distinguish an explicitly split calculation that resolves the bump from a missed-bump diagnostic; neither supplies a universal guarantee for all integrands. Compare an endpoint-derivative singularity before and after a change of variables, and retain evaluation/depth-budget exhaustion as an explicit termination status. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Gauss–Legendre and adaptive quadrature: exactness, error estimates and budgets Computation for a fixed target Construct Gaussian nodes/weights from the Legendre recurrence and test polynomial moments through degree 2n−1 and an exponential. Adaptive Simpson integrates exponential and Lorentzian peaks, against analytic integrals and independent QUADPACK. The local Simpson estimate is not a rigorous error bound for arbitrary functions. The implementation does not generally solve missed high frequencies, singularities or roundoff stagnation, and it is not a reimplementation of Gauss–Kronrod or all of QUADPACK. text.en: QUANTUM ATOMS · FIXED INPUTS · VERIFIED CODE Hydrogenic atoms and helium: runnable validation examples From analytic references to self-consistency: run hydrogenic radial equations and closed-shell HF / exchange-only LDA for helium, with measured errors and explicit limits. Two problem families; 23 packaged checks passed. The ZIP was independently extracted and its fixed-input calculations and figures reproduced. Shared execution and validation guide for Barnes–Hut, hydrogenic atoms and helium Wide tables and equations scroll horizontally. Atomic units: hartree for energy and bohr for distance. Nonrelativistic, infinite-mass point nuclei, isolated boundaries and second-order uniform radial differences. Helium is restricted to spherical 1s² with two electrons and no correlation energy. Hydrogenic atoms: check analytic energies and shapes [−12∂r2+l(l+1)2r2−Zr]unl=Enlunl,Enl=−Z22n2u(0)=u(rmax⁡)=0,∫∣u∣2dr=1 u=rR is the reduced radial orbital. H (Z=1) and He⁺ (Z=2) cover 1s, 2s, 2p and 3d states. Charge, state and resolution variants form one inventory problem family. Main runs use r_max=60 bohr and Δr=0.04, 0.02, 0.01 bohr. Hydrogen 1s at Δr=0.01 bohr. Overlapping profiles still have finite-grid error. ZnlE / hartreeE analytic / hartree|ΔE| / hartree 1.010-0.4999875006-0.50000000001.250e-05 1.020-0.1249992188-0.12500000007.812e-07 1.021-0.1250002604-0.12500000002.604e-07 1.032-0.0555555658-0.05555555561.028e-08 2.010-1.9998000400-2.00000000002.000e-04 2.020-0.4999875006-0.50000000001.250e-05 2.021-0.5000041669-0.50000000004.167e-06 2.032-0.2222223868-0.22222222221.646e-07 Checks cover normalization, 1s/2s orthogonality, Z² energy scaling and eigenpair residuals. Halving Δr gives an energy-error reduction of approximately four. Separate box truncation from mesh error The table fixes Δr=0.01 bohr for hydrogen 1s. Stabilizing the box size leaves a finite mesh error relative to the analytic energy. r_max / bohrE / hartree|E − E analytic| / hartree 4-0.48325156551.675e-02 8-0.49996259593.740e-05 16-0.49998750061.250e-05 32-0.49998750061.250e-05 Helium: self-consistent HF and exchange-only LDA p(r)=4πr2n(r)=2u(r)2,∫p dr=2vH(r)=∫p(s)max⁡(r,s)ds,EH=12∫pvH drvxLDA=−(3nπ)1/3,ExLDA=34∫pvxLDA drE=Ts+Vnuc+EH+Ex,Ec=0 n is positive electron number density. Only for this two-electron, single-spatial-orbital HF problem, exchange cancels half the Hartree term: v_eff=−2/r+v_H/2 and E_x=−E_H/2. General HF exchange is not a local potential. LDA here is spin-unpolarized Dirac exchange only, without VWN or other correlation. p(r)=4πr²n(r), distinct from the three-dimensional density n. Each profile integrates to two electrons. Compare with an independently computed reference A separate PySCF 2.11.0 script supplies Gaussian-basis HF and Libxc LDA_X references. Uncontracted s-Gaussian bases of 24, 32 and 40 functions and two LDA quadrature grids are checked. It imports no atlas SCF, Hartree or exchange function. Distinguish the finite-grid value, extrapolated estimate and finite-Gaussian/quadrature reference. Extrapolation is not a certified bound or the exact correlated-helium energy. Record SCF stopping rules and failures Linear density mixing uses 0.35. Convergence requires all three: input-output density L1 residual <10⁻⁹, energy change <10⁻¹⁰ hartree, and output-density orbital residual <10⁻⁷ hartree. An alternative initial density and mixing 0.7 are checked. Normalization imposes electron number, which is also tested. Not a general molecular, periodic or many-electron solver. Checks cover analytic states, charge scaling, orthogonality, a dense eigensolver, analytic exponential-density Hartree fields, exchange differentiation, grid/domain convergence, starts, failure and independent implementations. text.ja: ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE · QUANTUM CHEMISTRY · DFT 量子化学・DFT：何を近似し、何を解くか Schrödinger、HF・DFTから基底・SCF・電子相関へ。周期系の空間群、小群、既約表現、SOCと時間反転もたどる。 20項目の日英解説と36件の一次文献を公開。水素型原子・Heの2問題群と、H₂の限定した有限基底RHFに実行・検証例があります。周期He固定セルのLDA実行例も公開。一般の分子DFT・他の周期物質は未検証です。 最初に分けて考える3つのこと 物理モデル・近似 HF、KS-DFT、MP2、CI、CC等。どの多電子状態やエネルギーを近似するか。 表現・離散化 基底、格子、擬ポテンシャル、k点。モデルを有限の計算問題にする方法。 方程式の解き方 固有値計算、SCF、混合、DIIS。選んだ離散問題をどこまで解いたか。 「SCFが収束した」「基底が収束した」「物理モデルが妥当」は別の確認です。代表式は原子単位系（ℏ = m_e = e = 4πε₀ = 1）を用います。有限の分子と周期的な固体は境界条件も違います。 Schrödinger固有値問題 固定した核配置に対して電子の多体固有値問題を解く、という共通の出発点です。ここでは非相対論・Born–Oppenheimer近似・原子単位系を使い、電子エネルギーE_elと核間反発E_NNを分けます。R_Aは核位置、Z_Aは核電荷、r_ijは電子間距離です。 1電子なら電子間反発の和はなく、水素型原子は E_n = −Z²/(2n²) を参照値にできます。多電子のΨは全電子座標とスピンに依存するため、3次元の1電子軌道を解くHF・KSとの違いを意識します。 孤立水素型原子の1s・2s・2p・3dを一様動径格子で検証。多電子Schrödinger方程式全体の直接解法ではありません。 固定入力・コード・検証結果 H^el=−12∑i∇i2−∑iAZA∣ri−RA∣+∑i<j1rijH^elΨ=EelΨ,Etot=Eel+∑A<BZAZBRAB 長い式は横にスクロールできます。 核運動、相対論、スピン軌道相互作用、外場はこの代表式に含めません。固有値の残差が小さくても、領域・基底の誤差は残ります。 条件・実装状況・JSON Schrödinger, E. text.en: ELECTRONIC STRUCTURE · QUANTUM CHEMISTRY · DFT Quantum chemistry and DFT: approximations and equations From Schrödinger, HF and DFT to bases, SCF and correlation, including space groups, little-group irreps, SOC and time reversal in band calculations. Bilingual reading for 20 entries and 36 primary publications. Runnable validation covers two hydrogenic/He families and scoped finite-basis H₂ RHF. A fixed periodic-He LDA workflow is also available; general molecular DFT and other periodic materials remain unvalidated. Three choices to keep separate Physical model and approximation HF, KS-DFT, MP2, CI or CC: which many-electron states and energies are approximated? Representation and discretization Basis, grid, pseudopotential and k sampling: how is the model made finite? Equation solver Eigensolvers, SCF, mixing and DIIS: how accurately is the chosen discrete problem solved? SCF convergence, basis convergence and physical adequacy are distinct checks. Representative equations use atomic units (ℏ = m_e = e = 4πε₀ = 1). Finite molecules and periodic solids also require different boundaries. Schrodinger eigenproblems The common starting point is a many-electron eigenproblem at fixed nuclear positions. We use nonrelativistic Born–Oppenheimer theory and atomic units, separating electronic energy E_el from nuclear repulsion E_NN. R_A and Z_A denote nuclear positions and charges; r_ij is an electron–electron distance. For one electron the pair-repulsion sum vanishes; hydrogenic energies E_n = −Z²/(2n²) provide references. The many-electron wavefunction depends on all electronic coordinates and spins, unlike the individual three-dimensional orbitals in HF or KS. Uniform radial-grid tests of isolated hydrogenic 1s, 2s, 2p and 3d states; not a direct general many-electron Schrödinger solver. (1929) Band symmetry groups and irreducible representations A structural space group includes translations, rotations, mirrors, inversion and their combinations. Band classification must use the symmetries actually preserved by the Hamiltonian, including magnetic order, spin–orbit coupling (SOC) and external fields. A Seitz operation g = {R|τ} maps position to Rr + τ. With lattice translations T as a normal subgroup, G/T is the crystal point group. At each k, the little group G_k retains operations taking Rk back to k modulo a reciprocal vector K. Its little co-group G_k/T is distinct from the full crystal point group. g={R∣τ}: r↦Rr+τ,P=G/TGk={{R∣τ}∈G: Rk=k+K, K∈L∗} Long equations scroll horizontally. Read little-group irreps and degeneracies Symmetries act within the Bloch-state space associated with k. Irreducible small representations classify bands. Their dimensions constrain symmetry-required multiplicities; accidental coincidence and antiunitary pairing are additional possibilities. Nearly equal energies alone do not identify an irrep. Little groups change between high-symmetry points, lines and planes. Compatibility relations track representation branching and band connectivity. For a simple symmorphic mirror line without SOC, mirror eigenvalues +1 and −1 label distinct sectors that cannot hybridize while that symmetry is preserved. Screw axes, glide planes and nonsymmorphic groups Screw and glide operations include fractional translations. Bloch phases matter, particularly at zone boundaries, so ordinary crystal-point-group character tables are insufficient. Use little-group small representations or equivalent projective little-co-group representations with their factor systems. Nonsymmorphic symmetry can constrain degeneracies and connectivity. It does not imply that every band is degenerate at every k: specify the group, k, spin and time-reversal conditions. ψnk(r+a)=eik⋅aψnk(r),a∈L SOC, double groups, time reversal and Kramers pairs Spin-1/2 SOC requires spinors that change sign under a 2π rotation, hence double-valued representations of double groups. Time reversal Θ is antiunitary with Θ² = −1 for electrons. Time reversal alone generally pairs k with −k; Kramers degeneracy at the same k is guaranteed at time-reversal-invariant momenta (TRIM), where 2k is reciprocal. In the usual nonmagnetic spin-1/2 setting with both inversion P and time reversal Θ, PΘ preserves each k and squares to −1, producing double degeneracy at each k. This conclusion cannot be transferred unchanged to a noncentrosymmetric system. Spinless Θ² = +1 models also do not satisfy these Kramers assumptions. text.ja: 放射輸送・モーメント法 放射輸送では位置・方向・周波数に依存する強度を解きます。角度を積分したモーメント法は未知数を減らしますが、失われた角度情報を閉包で補う必要があります。 対象と代表式 ここでは静止媒質・周波数積分済みの灰色強度Iを考え、等方な放射源ηと吸収係数κを使い、散乱は省略します。κは長さの逆数です。E=(1/c)∫I dΩ、F=∫nI dΩ、P=(1/c)∫nnI dΩを定義すると、EとFの方程式はPを含みます。 1c∂tI+n⋅∇I=η−κI,∂tE+∇⋅F=4πη−cκE,c−2∂tF+∇⋅P=−κF/c. 計算の流れ 離散方向法は角度を直接離散化し、モーメント法はP=D EのEddingtonテンソルを閉じます。M1は局所E,FからDを与える代表例で、FLDはFをEの勾配から表す別の近似です。光学的厚い極限と自由流の極限を照合し、物質との交換を同じエネルギー収支で計算します。 適用条件と落とし穴 M1は異なる方向の交差ビームを一般には独立に運べません。FLDは勾配方向に流束を結び付けるため影や強い異方性に制約があります。縮約光速は物理的な伝播/緩和時間を変えるので、支配的な時間尺度との関係を明示します。 追加版も1次元定常・純吸収・指定流入の平板で、μ∂xI=−κIを解きます。一般の放射モーメント閉包、散乱、時間依存、多周波数や流体との結合は検証しません。 検証するときに見る量 吸収だけの指数減衰、等方拡散、自由流と影、交差ビームを分けて調べます。E≥0、|F|≤cEという実現可能性、放射と物質の総エネルギー、角度/空間/時間収束を確認します。閉包誤差と離散化誤差を混同しません。 Beer–Lambertの各ray解析解と連続角度の指数積分を使い、固定角度での風上空間誤差と、厳密ray伝播での角度求積誤差を分離します。流入−流出と体積吸収の収支・正値性を別に確認し、保存則だけで角度分布の精度を判定しません。 光学的厚さ0.1・0.7・3で、連続角度参照を指数積分expnと別の適応QUADPACK求積でも照合します。独立な輸送標本化では入射fluxに対応するμ=√Uを用い、透過をBernoulli変数として数えます。64反復の有限標本で二項信頼区間とRMSEを調べますが、公称95%の被覆を任意の入力や標本で保証したとは表示しません。 固定入力で確かめる：別々の配布版 各例の入力・観測量・診断の定義と適用範囲を確認します。検査の合格が示す内容は受入条件によって異なり、数学的な一般保証とは区別します。旧版の入力・測定・公差は保持します。 純吸収平板の離散座標放射輸送 固定した標的の計算例 純吸収の定常放射輸送を角度と空間で離散化し、Beer–Lambert解と積分された出射フラックスで検証します。 多重散乱、熱放射、周波数再分配、動的媒質、放射流体連成は未実装です。StamnesらのDISORTの全機能・安定化を再現したとは表示しません。 入力・結果・受入条件 · 手法・式・一次文献 · コード：run.py · コード：electrostatics.py · コード：fmm.py · コード：transport.py · テスト：test_particles.py · 配布ZIP · 保存結果 · 独立展開からの追試記録 放射輸送：空間・角度収束と光子統計 固定した標的の計算例 純吸収平板で特性解・独立適応求積・光子生存率を比較し、離散収支と標本誤差・区間被覆を別々に測ります。 区間被覆は有限の固定seedでの観測で、ちょうど95%の実測値や全seedの成功を保証しません。決定論的求積誤差を統計誤差へ含めず、多重散乱・周波数依存・熱放射・放射流体連成は未検証です。 text.en: Radiation transport and moment methods Radiation transport resolves intensity in space, direction and frequency. Moment methods reduce the angular dimension but require closure for information removed by integration. Problem and representative equations Use frequency-integrated grey intensity I in a static medium, with isotropic emissivity η and absorption coefficient κ of inverse-length units; omit scattering here. Define E=(1/c)∫I dΩ, F=∫nI dΩ and P=(1/c)∫nnI dΩ. Moment equations for E and F require a prescription for P. 1c∂tI+n⋅∇I=η−κI,∂tE+∇⋅F=4πη−cκE,c−2∂tF+∇⋅P=−κF/c. Algorithm Discrete ordinates discretizes angle directly; moment methods close P=D E. M1 obtains D locally from E and F, while flux-limited diffusion instead approximates F from the gradient of E. Check optically thick and free-streaming limits and couple matter exchange through a consistent energy balance. Conditions and pitfalls M1 generally cannot propagate crossing beams independently. FLD ties flux to the energy gradient, limiting shadows and strongly anisotropic fields. A reduced light speed changes transport/relaxation scales and must be justified against the physical time scales of interest. The companion retains a one-dimensional steady purely absorbing slab with specified inflow, solving μ∂xI=−κI. General radiation moment closures, scattering, time dependence, multiple frequencies and fluid coupling are unvalidated. What to check Test exponential absorption, isotropic diffusion, free streaming/shadows and crossing beams separately. Check E≥0, |F|≤cE, matter-plus-radiation energy and angular/spatial/time convergence. Distinguish closure error from discretization error. Use directional Beer–Lambert solutions and a continuum-angle exponential integral, separating upwind spatial error at fixed ordinates from angular-quadrature error with exact ray propagation. Check inflow–outflow versus volume absorption and positivity separately; a balance check alone does not establish angular-distribution accuracy. At optical depths 0.1/0.7/3, cross-check the continuum-angle reference using expn and a separate adaptive QUADPACK quadrature. Independent transport sampling draws μ=√U for the incident flux and counts transmission as a Bernoulli variable. Check binomial intervals and RMSE over 64 finite-sample replicates; nominal 95% coverage is not claimed for arbitrary inputs or samples. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Discrete-ordinate radiation transport through an absorbing slab Computation for a fixed target Discretize steady pure-absorption transfer in angle and space, checking Beer–Lambert rays and integrated exit flux. Multiple scattering, thermal emission, frequency redistribution, moving media and radiation–fluid coupling are unimplemented. This does not reproduce full DISORT functionality/stabilization. Input, results and acceptance · Method, equations and sources · Code: run.py · Code: electrostatics.py · Code: fmm.py · Code: transport.py · Tests: test_particles.py · Release ZIP · Saved results · Independent-extraction rerun receipt Radiation transport: space/angle convergence and photon statistics Computation for a fixed target Compare characteristics, independent adaptive integration and photon survival in a pure-absorption slab; separate discrete balance, sampling error and interval coverage. Coverage is observed over finite fixed seeds; neither exactly 95% empirical coverage nor all-seed success is guaranteed. Keep deterministic quadrature error separate from statistical error. Multiple scattering, frequency dependence, thermal emission and radiation hydrodynamics are unvalidated. text.ja: 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。 Euler再構成：PPM・特性変数・WENO-Z・AUSM 計算済み比較を開く。1次元で再構成と数値流束を区別して調べます。従来の成分ごとのMUSCL／WENO基準例を残して拡張します。 比較するもの# 再構成表示では、保存変数成分／特性変数でのMUSCL・MC、制限付き放物線有限体積、有限差分WENO5-JS／Zを比較します。FVはHLLC、FDは大域Lax–Friedrichs流束分離を使い、ともにSSPRK3、公称CFL 0.3、同じ格子点数です。表現・流束・誤差ノルムが異なり、再構成だけの比較や同じ計算費用での順位ではありません。各手法内で基底だけを変える比較は条件を揃えています。 別の流束表示は保存特性変数MUSCL・MCとSSPRK3を固定し、HLLC、音響エントロピー修正付きRoe、Einfeldt型HLLE、後述のAUSM基準例を切り替えます。 制限付き放物線有限体積# Colella–Woodward（1984）の再構成の考え方に沿い、セル平均と両端値から放物線を作ります。確認した公開資料は1982年の著者プレプリントで、最終学術誌版とは異なります。本実装は端値補間・単調性制約を含み、method of linesでSSPRK3と結合します。この経路には波追跡・接触面急峻化・衝撃波平坦化を含めません。それらを加えた直接Euler型は第2段階で提供します。Lagrange発展・remapは今後の課題です。 セル平均Q、端値L,R、ξ∈[0,1]として、 q(ξ)=L+ξ[R−L+q6(1−ξ)],q6=6Q−3(L+R). とすれば、積分平均は厳密にQです。隣接平均の範囲で端値を制限し、極値を平坦化して曲率制約を適用します。セル内で固定した保存変数の特性基底へ偏差を射影し、制限して戻します。「成分」は基本変数ではなく保存変数です。必要なら左端・中点・右端にQまわりの共通の正値縮小を施し、Simpson平均Qを保ちます。保存平均をクリップせず、不正なRK段階では時間刻みを半分にして再試行します。完全離散正値性の一般的証明ではありません。 特性変数の有限差分WENO-Z# 各面でRoe平均の保存変数特性基底を固定します。正負の大域LF分離流束を射影し、特性成分ごとに再構成して面流束へ戻します。FDは点値を進める方式で、FVの状態再構成とは異なります。周期格子では共有流束差分により離散和を保存します。 Z変種はJSの滑らかさ指標を使い、 τ5=∣β0−β2∣,αkZ=dk[1+(τ5βk+ϵ)2],ωkZ=αkZ∑lαlZ,(d0,d1,d2)=(0.1,0.6,0.3). とします。ε=10⁻⁶、Zの指数2を固定します。正則化と特性基底の規格化は重みに影響するため、比較条件に含めます。原典の書誌はBorges・Carmona・Costa・Don（2008）です。出版社メタデータと以前の3著者の草稿を確認しましたが、草稿は重みの規約が異なります。上の式・指数と実行検証が本版の変種を定義し、最終論文の図は再現していません。 AUSMは変種を明示する# AUSMの原典はLiou–Steffen（1993）です。本基準例は共通面音速a=(aL+aR)/2、亜音速のMach分割M±=±(M±1)²/4、3次圧力分割P±=(M±1)²(2∓M)/4を使います。超音速側は符号に従う風上分割です。式はFEST-3Dの公式AUSMソースと照合しました。定義を明示した独立のAUSM系列実装であり、FEST-3Dの計算結果や1993年の全音速・圧力選択肢の再現ではありません。 Mf=M+(uL/a)+M−(uR/a)を使い、(ρ,ρu,ρv,ρH)を左のa max(Mf,0)と右のa min(Mf,0)で輸送します。pL P+(uL/a)+pR P−(uR/a)を法線運動量だけに加え、エネルギーには全エンタルピーを輸送します。一様場、両向き超音速、Mach ±1の分岐、静止・移動接触面、Euler問題を検証します。 AUSM+（1996）、AUSM+-up（2006）は新しい波追跡PPM比較で別々に定義しています。現基準例に全速度補正や低Mach検証はありません。名称だけで普遍的な衝撃波安定性は導けません。odd–even比較も参照してください。 問題・参照・精度# Sod：N=200、[0,1]、t=0.2、標準状態、外挿端。 移動接触面：N=200、周期[0,1]、u=p=1、前半の密度1・後半2、1周t=1。 Shu–Osher：N=240、[−5,5]、t=1.8、固定端。x=−4の左は(ρ,u,p)=(3.857143,2.629369,10.33333)、右は密度1+0.2sin(5x)、u=0,p=1。破線は本実装の特性FD WENO-Z・N=960で、厳密解や外部コード検証ではありません。 FVの初期値は保存量を積分します。Sodの最終密度誤差は解析リーマン解の128点Gauss求積を使い、64／128点の差で不連続を跨ぐ求積感度を記録します。FD誤差は点値です。FV基本変数曲線は保存平均からの変換で、基本変数そのものの厳密平均ではありません。Shu–Osherの厳密誤差は報告しません。 別の滑らかな周期エントロピー波をN=32,64,128、t=0.2、CFL=0.25(32/N)^(2/3)で計算します。dt∝dx^(5/3)によりSSPRK3の時間誤差をO(dx⁵)へ抑えます。この問題のWENO観測次数は約5、極値制限のある放物線FVは約2です。衝撃波や任意の臨界点での5次精度保証ではありません。 再現はpython scripts/build_reconstruction.pyです。分布・診断・ソースハッシュと保存変数配列を取得できます。正値性・再試行回数は、ここで示したテストの範囲です。 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM Open the computed comparison. This 1D experiment separates reconstruction choices from numerical-flux choices. It extends the original componentwise MUSCL/WENO baseline; previous exhibits are retained. What is compared# The reconstruction view compares conservative-component and characteristic MUSCL/MC, limited parabolic finite volumes, and finite-difference WENO5-JS/Z. FV uses HLLC; FD uses global Lax–Friedrichs flux splitting. Both use SSPRK3, nominal CFL 0.3 and the same number of grid locations. Their representations, fluxes and error norms differ: this is not an isolated reconstruction or matched-cost ranking. Within each method, changing only the basis is a controlled component/characteristic comparison. The separate flux view fixes conservative characteristic MUSCL/MC and SSPRK3, then switches HLLC, acoustic-smoothed Roe, Einfeldt-type HLLE and the explicitly defined AUSM baseline below. It does not change the spatial reconstruction. Limited parabolic finite volumes# Following the reconstruction idea of Colella–Woodward (1984), form a parabola in each cell from its mean and two edges. The inspected public 1982 author preprint is an earlier version, not the final journal layout. This implementation includes limited edge interpolation and monotonicity constraints, coupled by method of lines to SSPRK3. It excludes original PPM wave tracing, contact steepening, shock flattening, Lagrangian evolution and remap. Direct-Eulerian tracing, contact steepening and flattening are now available in the second computed stage; Lagrangian evolution and remap remain future work. For a cell mean Q and edges L,R, use the local coordinate ξ in [0,1]: q(ξ)=L+ξ[R−L+q6(1−ξ)],q6=6Q−3(L+R). The integral is exactly Q. Limit initial edge interpolation between adjacent means; flatten a parabolic extremum and apply the usual curvature bounds. Characteristic projection freezes a local conservative eigenbasis in each cell, limits projected deviations, then transforms back. Components are conservative variables, not primitive variables. Reconstructed left/mid/right states share one affine positivity scaling about Q if needed. Their Simpson mean remains Q; no conserved mean is clipped. Inadmissible RK stages retry with a halved time step. These safeguards do not prove fully discrete positivity. Characteristic finite-difference WENO-Z# For each face freeze a Roe-averaged conservative eigenbasis. Project the positive and negative global-LF split flux stencils, reconstruct each characteristic component, and transform the resulting face flux back. FD evolves point values; it is not FV state reconstruction. Shared flux differences conserve the discrete sum on a periodic grid. The Z variant uses the JS smoothness indicators with τ5=∣β0−β2∣,αkZ=dk[1+(τ5βk+ϵ)2],ωkZ=αkZ∑lαlZ,(d0,d1,d2)=(0.1,0.6,0.3). Here ε = 10⁻⁶ is fixed and the Z exponent is 2. These choices must accompany comparisons; the regularization and normalization of the characteristics affect the weights. Borges, Carmona, Costa and Don (2008) is the original bibliographic reference. Publisher metadata and the public earlier three-author manuscript were inspected; that manuscript has different weight conventions. The formula above, its exponent and the executable checks define this edition's variant; no final-paper figure is reproduced. AUSM: keep the variant explicit# Liou–Steffen (1993) introduced AUSM. The local baseline uses a common interface sound speed a = (aL+aR)/2, Mach polynomials M± = ±(M±1)²/4 in the subsonic interval, and the cubic pressure fractions P± = (M±1)²(2∓M)/4. Supersonic branches use signed upwind Mach and pressure fractions. These formulas were cross-checked against the official FEST-3D AUSM source. This is an independently implemented, specified AUSM-family variant, not FEST-3D output or a reproduction of every 1993 sound-speed/pressure option. Let Mf = M+(uL/a)+M−(uR/a). Upwind the advected vector (ρ,ρu,ρv,ρH) using a max(Mf,0) on the left and a min(Mf,0) on the right, and add pL P+(uL/a)+pR P−(uR/a) to normal momentum only. Energy transports total enthalpy. Tests include uniform states, both supersonic directions, Mach ±1 branch limits, stationary/moving contacts and the computed Euler problems. AUSM+ (1996) and AUSM+-up (2006) are separately defined in the new traced-PPM comparison. The current baseline has no all-speed correction or low-Mach verification. None of these names implies universal shock stability; inspect the separate odd–even comparison. Problems, references and accuracy# Sod: N=200, x∈[0,1], t=0.2, standard states, extrapolated ends. Moving contact: N=200, periodic [0,1], u=p=1, density 1 on the first half and 2 on the second; one crossing t=1. Shu–Osher: N=240, x∈[−5,5], t=1.8, fixed end states, shock at −4, left (ρ,u,p)=(3.857143,2.629369,10.33333), right density 1+0.2sin(5x), u=0,p=1. The dashed curve is our internal characteristic FD WENO-Z N=960 run, not an exact solution or an external-code validation. FV initialization integrates conserved quantities. Sod final density errors use 128-node Gauss quadrature of the analytic Riemann solution; the saved 64/128-node discrepancy estimates quadrature sensitivity across discontinuities. FD errors are pointwise. Derived FV primitive curves are primitive variables of conserved means, not exact primitive means. No exact Shu–Osher error is reported. A separate smooth periodic entropy wave uses N=32,64,128 at t=0.2 and CFL = 0.25(32/N)^(2/3). This reduces dt proportional to dx^(5/3), making the SSPRK3 time error O(dx⁵). Measured WENO orders are about five on this smooth case; limited PPM is about two on this sequence because of extremum limiting. This is not a global fifth-order guarantee at shocks or arbitrary critical points. Reproduce with python scripts/build_reconstruction.py. Download profiles, diagnostics and source hashes and conserved arrays. The final arrays, positive-state checks and retry counts apply only to the stated tests. Historical atlas →Computed gallery →

ja.title: 点値と有限体積セル平均#

text.ja: 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 英語原文が更新されています。この日本語訳は旧版に対応します。 厳密解・参照解ライブラリ 検証用ライブラリでは「正解」が何を意味するかを明示します。参照解エクスプローラーには、式、仮定、出典、点値、1次元ではセル平均を備えた18ケースを収録しています。参照解を評価する機能であり、数値的なPDEの時間発展は行いません。 4種類の参照解# 解析解（analytic）：スカラーのエントロピー波、正弦波の移流・減衰、乾床・真空への膨張波、チャネル流、Taylor–Green流などの陽な式です。浮動小数点評価の丸め誤差は残ります。 半解析解（semi-analytic）：Euler、水深が正の浅水流、等温流のRiemann解です。波の曲線は解析的ですが、中間状態の接続にはスカラー方程式の数値的な求根が必要です。 製造解（manufactured）：滑らかな場を先に与え、外力と境界条件を導きます。Poissonの正弦波ケースは、その場に合わせて選んだ強制問題を検証します。 数値参照解（numerical reference）：細かい格子などで計算した数値解です。離散化・境界・時間積分の誤差が残ります。既存アトラスの高解像度比較は、該当する場合にこの区分を明示します。本ライブラリの解析解ケースとしては追加していません。 参照解との一致は、特定の設定についての実装検証です。実験との比較による物理モデルの妥当性確認や、任意の境界処理の保証とは異なります。 収録する場と仮定# スカラーには周期正弦波の移流と熱減衰、Burgersの衝撃波・膨張波、2次交通流モデルの衝撃波・膨張波があります。EulerにはSod、Lax、二重膨張波、生成される真空を収録し、比熱比1.4の理想気体を使います。浅水流には水深が正のダム崩壊、乾床への膨張、中央の乾燥領域を収録し、平坦な底面と重力1を使います。等温Eulerは一定音速1、初期密度は厳密に正とし、エネルギー方程式や有限の真空状態を持ちません。 粘性流は単位幅の平面チャネルにおける定常Couette・Poiseuille速度分布と、周期的な2次元Taylor–Green渦です。チャネルの出力は速度であり、圧縮流の保存変数ではありません。Taylor–Greenは速度と平均ゼロに固定した圧力を返します。Poisson製造解は場と外力の両方を提供します。 いずれも標準的な無次元設定です。参照解の乾床・真空への対応は、既存の正値状態を要求する有限体積ソルバーに、その機能を追加するものではありません。地形、粘性Riemann問題、一般の状態方程式、多次元衝撃波相互作用は初回の対象外です。 点値と有限体積セル平均# 保存変数を有限体積法で比較するときは、次のセル平均を使います。 U‾i(t)=1xi+1/2−xi−1/2∫xi−1/2xi+1/2U(x,t) dx. Eulerでは密度・運動量・全エネルギー、浅水・等温流では水深または密度と運動量を積分します。保存変数の平均を基本変数に変換したものは、一般に基本変数自体の平均とは異なります。衝撃波がセルを横切るとき、セル中心の点値で代用すると特に誤解を招きます。 既知の衝撃波・接触面・膨張波の両端で積分区間を滑らかな部分に分け、各部分に24点と48点のGauss–Legendre積分を適用します。保存する平均は48点の結果です。両次数の最大差は収束の目安であり、厳密な誤差上限ではありません。この規則は解析解にも適用し、保存セル平均は記号積分ではなく有限次数の求積で計算します。 非一様格子での誤差ノルムは全領域長で規格化します。 L1=∑iΔxi∣ei∣∑iΔxi,L2=(∑iΔxiei2∑iΔxi)1/2,L∞=max⁡i∣ei∣. 成分ごとに報告します。方程式ギャラリーのEuler・浅水・等温流にも、これらの保存変数セル平均を接続しました。保存時刻の数値解は引き続き、最終時刻を変えて独立に実行した計算です。 Riemann解の構成と許容誤差# 自己相似変数xi=(x−x0)/tを使います。接続する未知量はEulerでは圧力、浅水では水深、等温流では密度です。正の未知量の対数に対して単調な波接続残差を挟み込み、二分法を適用します。対数区間幅の目標は2e−13、二分法は最大160回、最終残差は特性速度スケールの2e−10倍以内であることを検査します。残差が厳密にゼロなら、それ以前に停止できます。反復回数、最終区間幅、残差をケースごとに保存します。 Eulerや浅水の膨張波が離れると、中央に真空・乾燥領域が生じる場合があります。その場合は正状態の求根を省略します。保存変数はすべてゼロです。真空中の速度は物理的に未定義ですが、低レベルの変換では表示上の規約としてゼロとします。等温流では有限の真空の代わりに、非常に小さい正の密度になります。float64の対応範囲を超える状態は、黙って切り詰めずエラーにします。 ClawpackのEulerの章と浅水の章は、波の構成と乾床・真空を説明しています。Bhat・Fetecauの著者原稿のRiemann問題の議論には、元の等温Euler系の波曲線があります。本ライブラリは、その元の系を使い、論文の正則化モデルは使いません。 粘性流と製造解の式# 単位幅・単位密度・動粘性係数nuの平面チャネルでは、定常分布は次式です。 uCouette(y)=y,uPoiseuille(y)=G2νy(1−y),G=1,ν=0.1. Couetteでは壁速度が0と1、圧力勾配はゼロです。Poiseuilleでは両壁が静止したno-slip条件で、Gは密度で割った負の圧力勾配、または等価な体積力加速度です。十分に発達した平面流であり、円管流ではありません。 周期正方形[0,2pi]²のTaylor–Green解は、nu=0.1、単位密度で次のとおりです。 u=sin⁡xcos⁡y e−2νt,v=−cos⁡xsin⁡y e−2νt,p=cos⁡(2x)+cos⁡(2y)4e−4νt. Webではy=pi/4のx方向断面を表示し、2次元セル面積平均ではありません。Pythonは2次元座標と滑らかな長方形セルの平均に対応します。関連する方法は粘性流の章を参照してください。 製造解はu=sin(pi x)を与え、−u_xx=f=pi² sin(pi x)、両端は同次Dirichlet条件とします。同じオブジェクトから外力を取得できます。任意の外力に対するPoissonソルバーではありません。 再利用と再現# import numpy as np from numart.reference_solutions import get_reference, riemann_reference ref = get_reference('euler-sod') edges = np.array([0., .15, .42, .51, .7, 1.]) points = ref.point((edges[:-1] + edges[1:]) / 2, t=.2) report = ref.cell_average_report(edges, t=.2) means = report['values'] # columns: rho, rho*u, E # With actual numerical conserved means q of the same shape: # errors = ref.compare_means(q, edges, t=.2) custom = riemann_reference('shallow-water', (2., 0.), (1., 0.), parameter=9.81) tg = get_reference('taylor-green') box_mean = tg.box_average([0., 0.], [.2, .3], t=.5) 保存分布と図はMPLCONFIGDIR=.mplconfig python scripts/build_reference_solutions.pyで再生成できます。データと数値実装のソースハッシュをダウンロード。Pythonでは、既存の独立なEuler実装との比較、Rankine–Hugoniot条件とLax不等式、膨張波のPDE残差と不変量、全領域の収支、既知の積分、製造解の外力、Taylor–Greenの運動量・発散残差を検証します。Webのビルドでは保存データの形式、波の位置、ソースハッシュ、平均値の規約を検査します。 Blasius、Sedov、Nohや追加の多次元参照解は今後の拡張です。LANL ExactPackはそれらを追加する際に参照できる独立した資料集です。現時点の依存ライブラリではなく、上のケースをExactPackと相互検証したという意味でもありません。 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Exact and reference solutions A verification library should say what its answer means. The reference explorer contains 18 cases with formulas, assumptions, source links, point values and, for one-dimensional cases, cell means. It evaluates references; it does not advance a numerical PDE solution. Four different reference categories# Analytic: explicit formulas, including scalar entropy waves, sine translation/decay, dry-bed and vacuum fans, channel profiles and Taylor–Green flow. Floating-point evaluation still has rounding error. Semi-analytic: Euler, wet shallow-water and isothermal Riemann solutions. The wave curves are analytic, but matching the middle state requires a numerical scalar root solve. Manufactured: prescribe a smooth field and derive the forcing and boundary conditions. The Poisson sine case tests a forced problem chosen for that field. Numerical reference: a refined numerical computation. It retains discretization, boundary and time-integration errors. Existing high-resolution atlas comparisons belong here when explicitly identified; they are not additional analytic cases in this library. Agreement with a reference verifies a particular setup. It does not validate a physical model against experiments or certify every boundary treatment. Included fields and assumptions# The scalar cases are periodic sine advection and heat decay, Burgers shock/fan and quadratic traffic shock/fan. Euler includes Sod, Lax, a double rarefaction and a generated vacuum, all for an ideal gas with gamma 1.4. Shallow water includes a wet dam break, expansion into a dry bed and a dry middle state, with a flat bottom and gravity 1. Isothermal Euler uses constant sound speed 1 and strictly positive initial density; it has no energy equation and no finite vacuum state. The viscous cases are planar steady Couette and Poiseuille profiles in a unit channel and a periodic two-dimensional Taylor–Green vortex. Channel profiles are velocity fields, not compressible conserved states. Taylor–Green returns velocity and pressure with a fixed zero-mean pressure gauge. The Poisson manufactured sine returns both the field and its forcing. These are canonical, nondimensional setups. Dry-bed/vacuum support in the reference evaluator does not add that capability to the existing positive-state finite-volume solver. Topography, viscosity in Riemann problems, arbitrary equations of state and multidimensional shock interactions are outside this first library. Point values and finite-volume means# For a conserved state, a finite-volume comparison uses U‾i(t)=1xi+1/2−xi−1/2∫xi−1/2xi+1/2U(x,t) dx. The library integrates density, momentum and total energy for Euler, and depth/density and momentum for shallow-water/isothermal flow. Converting a mean conserved state to primitive variables is generally different from averaging primitive variables. A shock cutting a cell makes a center sample particularly misleading. Known shocks, contacts and both edges of rarefaction fans split each integral into smooth pieces. Gauss–Legendre quadrature uses 24 and 48 points per piece; saved means use the 48-point result. The maximum difference between the two orders is a convergence estimate, not a rigorous error bound. This convention also applies to analytic cases: their saved cell means use finite-order quadrature rather than symbolic integration. For a nonuniform mesh, the reported error norms are normalized by total domain length: L1=∑iΔxi∣ei∣∑iΔxi,L2=(∑iΔxiei2∑iΔxi)1/2,L∞=max⁡i∣ei∣. Each component is reported separately. The Euler/SWE/isothermal equation gallery now uses these conserved cell means. Its saved physical times still come from independent final-time numerical solves. Riemann construction and tolerances# The self-similar solution uses xi=(x−x0)/t. For Euler the matched unknown is pressure; for shallow water it is depth; for isothermal flow it is density. The implementation brackets a monotone wave-matching residual in the logarithm of that positive unknown, then bisects. The target logarithmic bracket width is 2e−13, with at most 160 bisections and a final residual check of 2e−10 times a characteristic velocity scale. An exact zero residual can terminate earlier. Iterations, final bracket width and residual are saved alongside each case. Separating Euler or shallow-water fans can create a middle vacuum/dry region. Those cases bypass the positive-state root solve. Conserved variables vanish there. Velocity is physically undefined in vacuum; the low-level conversion displays zero by convention. Isothermal expansion approaches arbitrarily small positive density instead of a finite vacuum. States outside the supported float64 range raise an error rather than silently clipping the reference. The Clawpack Euler chapter and shallow-water chapter describe the wave construction and dry/vacuum cases. Bhat and Fetecau's author manuscript gives the isothermal wave curves for the original Euler system in its Riemann-problem discussion; this library uses that original system, not the paper's regularized model. Viscous and manufactured formulas# For a unit-height channel, unit density and viscosity nu, the steady profiles are uCouette(y)=y,uPoiseuille(y)=G2νy(1−y),G=1,ν=0.1. Couette has wall speeds 0 and 1 with zero pressure gradient. Poiseuille has stationary no-slip walls; G is either the negative pressure gradient per unit density or an equivalent body acceleration. These are fully developed planar flows, not pipe flow. For Taylor–Green on the periodic square [0,2pi]², with nu=0.1 and unit density, u=sin⁡xcos⁡y e−2νt,v=−cos⁡xsin⁡y e−2νt,p=cos⁡(2x)+cos⁡(2y)4e−4νt. The Web explorer displays an x-slice at y=pi/4, not two-dimensional area means. The Python evaluator accepts full 2D coordinates and smooth rectangular box averages. Related methods are in the viscous-flow chapter. The manufactured case prescribes u=sin(pi x), giving −u_xx=f=pi² sin(pi x) with homogeneous Dirichlet endpoints. Its source is available through the same object; it is not an arbitrary-source Poisson solver. Reuse and reproduce# import numpy as np from numart.reference_solutions import get_reference, riemann_reference ref = get_reference('euler-sod') edges = np.array([0., .15, .42, .51, .7, 1.]) points = ref.point((edges[:-1] + edges[1:]) / 2, t=.2) report = ref.cell_average_report(edges, t=.2) means = report['values'] # columns: rho, rho*u, E # With actual numerical conserved means q of the same shape: # errors = ref.compare_means(q, edges, t=.2) custom = riemann_reference('shallow-water', (2., 0.), (1., 0.), parameter=9.81) tg = get_reference('taylor-green') box_mean = tg.box_average([0., 0.], [.2, .3], t=.5) Rebuild the saved profiles and figure with MPLCONFIGDIR=.mplconfig python scripts/build_reference_solutions.py. Download the data and numerical source hashes. Python tests compare Euler with an existing independent implementation, check Rankine–Hugoniot jumps and Lax inequalities, rarefaction PDE residuals and invariants, global balances, known integrals, manufactured forcing and Taylor–Green momentum/divergence residuals. The Web build checks the saved schema, wave locations, source hashes and averaging conventions. Blasius, Sedov, Noh and additional multidimensional references remain future extensions. LANL ExactPack is an independent source collection to consult for those additions; it is not a dependency or a claim of cross-validation for the cases above. Historical atlas →Computed gallery →

text.en: LEARNING RESOURCES公開コード・データ / Public code and data References by original publication year Original papers and books are distinguished from sources used to check the implementations. A DOI does not imply that the full text has been inspected or its figures reproduced. Each note identifies publicly available originals, later expositions, and original sources that still need verification. NASA case resources appear in the 2D case catalog. This file and references.bib are generated from catalog/references.json by python scripts/build_references.py. 1847 · verhulst1847# Verhulst, Pierre-François. Sur la loi d’accroissement de la population (Deuxième mémoire). Mémoires de l’Académie royale de Belgique. Original bibliographic record · Full text or implementation reference Original archival text and metadata available. This is the later 1847 memoir, read in 1846; it must not be labeled the original 1838 logistic note. The early note is not audited in this survey. 1913 · michaelis1913# Michaelis, Leonor and Menten, Maud L.. Die Kinetik der Invertinwirkung. Biochemische Zeitschrift. Original bibliographic record · Full text or implementation reference Original 1913 bibliographic identification through the explicitly labeled Johnson–Goody 2011 translation. This URL identifies the translation, not a 1913 DOI. Original German text not audited; rapid-equilibrium and later quasi-steady-state interpretations are distinguished. 1920 · lotka1920# Lotka, Alfred J.. Analytical Note on Certain Rhythmic Relations in Organic Systems. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Original bibliographic record · Full text or implementation reference Original bibliographic record checked. Early rhythmic organic-system model, before the 1925 book and independent Volterra 1926 source. The survey gives a conventional normalized predator–prey system, not a reproduction of the original figures. 1925 · briggs1925# Briggs, George E. and Haldane, J. B. S.. ja.title: 既存Eulerから何が変わるか#
1972〜1998年：曲がった背景から保存的HRSCへ#
2013年以降：放射と微視的物理による硬い系#
並行する1979〜2019年の分岐：因果的な粘性流体#
2022〜2025年：衝撃波・表面・物理制約を伴う高次法#
アトラスで段階的に再現できること#

en.title: What changes from the existing Euler examples?#
1972–1998: from curved-background flows to conservative HRSC#
2013 onward: radiation and microphysics add stiff systems#
A parallel 1979–2019 branch: causal viscous fluid theory#
2022–2025: high order with shocks, surfaces, and physical constraints#
2025–2026: portable GPU computation of the coupled system#
What the atlas can reproduce in stages#

text.ja: 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 日本語訳はドラフトです。数式・計算・参照資料は英語原文と照合できます。 相対論的流体力学：SRHD、GRHD、GRMHD 2026年11月6日確認の文献調査。 アトラスのNewton力学的Eulerライブラリには未実装です。保存的衝撃波捕獲、曲がった・動く幾何、磁場制約、物理状態回復、高次法、放射、可搬並列計算が相互に発展してきました。出版、プレプリント、受理の年を区別する、選定した読書の道案内であり、網羅調査やコードの順位ではありません。 既存Eulerから何が変わるか# SRHDは平坦時空の相対論的物質、GRHDは与えた、またはEinstein方程式で進める曲がった計量、GRMHDは電磁寄与も扱います。Kerr背景の降着と動的時空の連星中性子星では、検証する系が異なります。 c=G=1、計量符号(−,+,+,+)の理想流体方程式は、 ∇μ(ρ0uμ)=0,∇μTμν=0,Tμν=ρ0huμuν+pgμν,h=1+ϵ+pρ0. です。rho0は静止質量密度、epsilonは比内部エネルギーです。直交SRHDの代表的な保存状態は、 W=(1−v2)−1/2,D=ρ0W,Si=ρ0hW2vi,τ=ρ0hW2−p−D. で、既存テストのNewton状態とは異なります。基本変数回復は非線形です。横速度ゼロの1次元音響速度もv±csではなく(v±cs)/(1±v cs)です。3+1 GRではlapse、shift、空間体積因子、計量微分が流束・ソースへ入ります。gammaの値の変更ではなく構造的な変化です。形式の総説はFont（2008）、Valenciaの原典は以下です。 1972〜1998年：曲がった背景から保存的HRSCへ# Wilson（1972）はKerrブラックホールへの気体落下の初期計算です。歴史的背景であり、固定背景流体が動的Einstein系全体を解くという意味ではありません。 高解像度衝撃波捕獲（HRSC）は古典CFDの特性・保存法を相対論へ移します。Martí・Müller（1994）の厳密SRリーマン解は初期不連続に垂直な流れを対象とします。横速度のある多次元テストでは範囲が重要で、一般の横流れリーマン解ではありません。 Banyulsら（1997）は、Valenciaと呼ばれる3+1局所特性形式を示します。保存状態、特性情報、幾何ソースによりGRへ現代的衝撃波捕獲を適用します。中心的な出典ですが、それ以前の全手法が非保存だったという主張ではありません。Ponsら（1998）は局所座標変換でGRHDとSRリーマンソルバーを結びます。局所求解の外では曲率・座標効果を別に扱います。 1999〜2006年：磁場制約と動的時空# Komissarov（1999）は磁束保存を持つ多次元Godunov型相対論MHDを開発します。HARM、Gammie–McKinney–Tóth（2003）は保存形GRMHD、HLL、Tóth型CTを組み合わせ、ブラックホールトーラスなどを計算します。原型と後の動的時空の枠組みを区別します。 Duezら（2005）は、時空にBSSN、物質に保存的衝撃波捕獲を使い、結合Einstein–Maxwell–MHDを進めます。物質と幾何が動的に影響し合うために必要な追加段階です。 保存変数でも物理状態の回復は必要です。Nobleら（2006）は1・2未知数への縮約を含む非線形回復を比較します。回復失敗、大気の下限、修復を、打切り誤差や保存変数残差と分けて追跡する必要があります。 2011〜2026年：GSPHからの粒子分岐# Inutsukaの原GSPHから、リーマン問題とAlfvén特性線を使うNewton粒子MHDのIwasaki–Inutsuka（2011）へ進みます。この方法自体は相対論的ではありません。 Kitajima–Inutsuka–Seno（2026）は**特殊相対論的Godunov SPH（SRGSPH）**を定式化します。畳み込み相互作用、不等バリオン数、可変平滑化長を、衝撃波管・Kelvin–Helmholtz例で扱い、粒子と相対論の分岐を直接つなぎます。プレプリントは2025年10月、掲載号は2026年1月で、DOIの2025表記と異なります。GRHD実装とは呼べません。 2013年以降：放射と微視的物理による硬い系# Sądowskiら（2013）は、半陰的相互作用ソースを持つKORALの共変M1放射モーメントを説明します。相対論流体とアトラスの陰解法・IMEXの計画をつなぎます。M1は角度モーメントの閉包で、放射分布全体を近似なしに解くものではありません。 中性子星合体についてFoucart（2023）は、leakage、モーメント、Monte Carloニュートリノ輸送と相互作用モデルの限界を総説します。有限温度EOS表、組成、輸送、不確かさはリーマン流束の選択とは別の発展です。理想相対論流体から、因果的な粘性理論が自動的に得られるわけでもありません。 並行する1979〜2019年の分岐：因果的な粘性流体# Newton流体の粘性応力を、因果性・初期値問題を調べずに相対論Eulerへ入れることはできません。Israel–Stewart（1979）は追加緩和変数を持つ過渡散逸理論の中心的出典です。 Bemfica–Disconzi–Noronha（2019）とKovtun（2019）は別の系譜で、適切な1階勾配の構成選択と流体フレームが、条件付きで因果的・安定な形式を可能にします。前者は追加拡張変数なしの非線形因果性、後者は安定な1階フレームを扱います。任意EOS・輸送に対する無条件の主張へ合体させてはいけません。物理因果性、PDEの適切性、離散刻みの安定性は別の検査です。理論・読書の背景で、粘性相対論ソルバーは未実装です。 2022〜2025年：衝撃波・表面・物理制約を伴う高次法# Deppeら（2022）は、高次DG更新を試し、不適切な領域を頑健な差分で再計算するDG–FD混合法です。2021年プレプリントと2022年出版を区別します。連星中性子星研究の2024年プレプリントは、動的時空・合体へ拡張します。後者はプレプリントとして引用し、別の学術誌記録は本調査では未確認です。 Cao–Peng–Wu（2025）は、GRHDの物理制約保存・振動除去DGを研究し、方式の仮定下で正の熱力学状態と光速未満の速度を扱います。任意の制限関数、流束、EOS、時空離散化への保証ではありません。選んだGRHD形式の定理と、天体合体コードの実演は別の根拠です。 2025〜2026年：結合系の可搬GPU計算# AthenaK、Fieldsら（2025）はGPU上の動的時空GRMHDと連星中性子星合体を実演し、CTと1次流束補正などを使います。プレプリントは2024年、学術誌はApJS 276、35（2025）です。AsterX、Kalinaniらの2025年掲載号も公開GPU向けGRMHDで、ValenciaとZ4cに基づきます。オンライン出版は2024年12月です。細分化基盤は原コードの一部で、このアトラスのAMRは引き続き保留です。 GRACE、Musolinoらは、11月6日確認時点で2026年11月2日にPhysical Review Dで受理されています。2026年7月プレプリントはKokkos可搬性、CT、Z4c結合、中性子星合体を説明します。受理は最終巻・ページの確認ではありません。これらは可搬実装の例であり、異なるハードウェア・物理間の普遍的な速度・精度順位ではありません。 アトラスで段階的に再現できること# 以下は実装案で、本調査の計算結果ではありません。 SRHD：基本・保存変数の往復、特性速度、滑らかな波、衝撃波管、反射、横速度例。EOSの有効性、正密度・正圧、光速未満を確認します。 SRMHD：相対論Alfvén波、磁場衝撃波管、ローターを加え、磁場発散演算子と全修復・下限を明示します。 固定計量GR：計量対応の平坦極限、Michel／Bondi降着、平衡星、トーラスを、幾何ソースの釣合いとともに確認します。 動的GR：独立検証した時空発展を結合し、合体の前にEinstein制約、バリオン保存、星の振動、波形収束を測ります。 放射またはSRGSPH：状態、境界、保存、輸送閉包、参照テストを各分岐で明示します。Newton例は比較に使い、相対論ソルバーが既にある根拠にはしません。 進歩はこれらの層の組合せから生まれます。新しい高次再構成や大きなGPU計算だけでは、基本変数回復、表面・大気処理、制約誤差、微視的物理の不確かさは解消しません。 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Relativistic hydrodynamics: SRHD, GRHD, and GRMHD Literature review, checked 6 November 2026. These methods are not implemented in the atlas's Newtonian Euler library. The development has several interacting branches: conservative shock capture, curved and evolving geometry, magnetic constraints, physical-state recovery, high-order methods, radiation, and portable parallel computation. Dates below distinguish publication from preprint and acceptance dates. This is a selected reading path, not an exhaustive review or a ranking of codes. What changes from the existing Euler examples?# SRHD evolves relativistic matter in flat spacetime. GRHD includes a curved metric, which may be prescribed or evolved with Einstein's equations. GRMHD also evolves the electromagnetic contribution. A Kerr-background accretion calculation and a binary-neutron-star calculation with dynamical spacetime therefore test different systems. With c = G = 1 and metric signature (-,+,+,+), ideal-fluid equations are ∇μ(ρ0uμ)=0,∇μTμν=0,Tμν=ρ0huμuν+pgμν,h=1+ϵ+pρ0. Here rho0 is rest-mass density and epsilon is specific internal energy. In Cartesian SRHD, a common conservative state is W=(1−v2)−1/2,D=ρ0W,Si=ρ0hW2vi,τ=ρ0hW2−p−D. It differs from the Newtonian state in the existing benchmarks. Primitive recovery is nonlinear. One-dimensional acoustic speeds with zero transverse velocity are (v +/- cs)/(1 +/- v cs), not v +/- cs. In a 3+1 GR formulation, lapse, shift, spatial volume factors, and metric derivatives enter the fluxes and sources. These are structural changes, not a different value of gamma. Font (2008) is the formulation review used here; the original Valencia reference is below. 1972–1998: from curved-background flows to conservative HRSC# Wilson (1972) is an early numerical study of gas falling into a Kerr black hole. It provides historical context for relativistic fluid computation, rather than a claim that fixed-background hydrodynamics solves the full evolving Einstein system. The high-resolution shock-capturing (HRSC) branch brings the characteristic and conservative methods of classical CFD into relativity. Martí and Müller (1994) give an exact SR Riemann solution for flow normal to the initial discontinuity. That scope matters when selecting multidimensional tests with transverse velocities; the original normal-flow reference is not a general transverse Riemann solution. Banyuls et al. (1997) present the 3+1 local characteristic formulation commonly called Valencia. Its conservative state, characteristic information, and geometric source terms make modern shock capture applicable in GR. It is a central reference, not a claim that all earlier relativistic methods were nonconservative. Pons et al. (1998) connect GRHD to SR Riemann solvers through a local coordinate transformation. Curvature and coordinate effects still have to be accounted for outside that local solve. 1999–2006: magnetic constraints and dynamical spacetime# Komissarov (1999) develops a multidimensional Godunov-type relativistic MHD scheme with magnetic flux conservation. HARM, Gammie–McKinney–Tóth (2003) combines conservative GRMHD, HLL fluxes, and a Tóth-type CT construction, with black-hole torus calculations among its examples. Its original formulation must be distinguished from later dynamical-spacetime frameworks. Duez et al. (2005) evolve the coupled Einstein–Maxwell–MHD system, using BSSN for spacetime and conservative shock capture for the matter. This is the additional step needed when matter and geometry affect one another dynamically. Conservation variables do not remove the need to recover physical fluid states. Noble et al. (2006) compare nonlinear recovery algorithms, including reductions to one or two unknowns. Recovery failure, atmosphere floors, and repairs must be tracked separately from truncation error and conserved-variable residuals. 2011–2026: the particle branch from GSPH# Inutsuka's original GSPH connects to Iwasaki–Inutsuka (2011), a Newtonian particle MHD method using Riemann problems and Alfvén characteristics. It is not itself relativistic. Kitajima–Inutsuka–Seno (2026) then formulate special relativistic Godunov SPH (SRGSPH). The paper addresses convolution-based interactions, unequal baryon numbers, and variable smoothing lengths, with shock-tube and Kelvin–Helmholtz examples. It is a direct bridge between the requested particle and relativistic branches. The preprint is from October 2025; the journal issue is January 2026, despite the DOI's 2025 identifier. It should not be described as a GRHD implementation. 2013 onward: radiation and microphysics add stiff systems# Sądowski et al. (2013) describe KORAL's covariant M1 radiation moments with semi-implicit interaction sources. This connects relativistic fluid methods to the atlas's planned implicit and IMEX chapters. M1 closes angular moments; it does not solve the full radiation distribution without approximation. For neutron-star mergers, Foucart (2023) reviews leakage, moment, and Monte Carlo neutrino transport and the remaining interaction-modeling limitations. Tabulated finite-temperature equations of state, composition, transport, and their uncertainties are separate advances from the choice of a Riemann flux. Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics also does not automatically supply a causal relativistic viscous theory. A parallel 1979–2019 branch: causal viscous fluid theory# The Newtonian viscous stress cannot simply be inserted into relativistic Euler equations without examining causality and the initial-value problem. Israel–Stewart (1979) provides a central reference for transient dissipative theories with additional relaxation variables. Bemfica–Disconzi–Noronha (2019) and Kovtun (2019) develop a different line: appropriate first-gradient constitutive choices and hydrodynamic frames can support causal or stable formulations under specified conditions. The former paper addresses nonlinear causality without extra extended variables; the latter examines stable first-order frames. Their results should not be merged into an unconditional claim for every equation of state or transport choice. Physical causality, PDE well-posedness, and stability of a discrete time step are separate checks. This branch is theory and reading context in the atlas, not an implemented viscous relativistic solver. 2022–2025: high order with shocks, surfaces, and physical constraints# Deppe et al. (2022) develop a DG–finite difference hybrid: attempt a high-order DG update and recompute inadmissible regions with robust FD. The 2021 preprint and 2022 publication dates should remain distinct. Their binary-neutron-star study (2024 preprint) extends the hybrid approach to dynamical spacetime and merger calculations. The latter is cited here as a preprint; a separate journal record has not been verified in this review. Cao–Peng–Wu (2025) study physical-constraint-preserving, oscillation-eliminating DG for GRHD, including positive thermodynamic states and subluminal velocity under their stated scheme assumptions. Their results are not a guarantee for arbitrary limiters, fluxes, EOS, or spacetime discretizations. A theorem for a selected GRHD formulation and an astrophysical merger-code demonstration are different types of evidence. 2025–2026: portable GPU computation of the coupled system# AthenaK, Fields et al. (2025) demonstrates dynamical-spacetime GRMHD and binary-neutron-star mergers on GPUs, with CT and first-order flux correction among its numerical ingredients. Its preprint is from 2024; the journal reference is ApJS 276, 35 (2025). AsterX, Kalinani et al. (2025 issue) provides another open GPU-oriented GRMHD framework, based on Valencia and Z4c. Its online publication was December 2024. Refinement infrastructure is part of those source codes; implementing AMR in this atlas remains deferred. GRACE, Musolino et al. was accepted by Physical Review D on 2 November 2026, as checked on 6 November. Its July 2026 preprint describes Kokkos-based portability, CT, Z4c coupling, and neutron-star merger examples. Acceptance is not a verified final volume/page citation. These papers establish examples of portable implementations; they do not establish a universal speed or accuracy ranking across hardware and physics. What the atlas can reproduce in stages# The following is an implementation proposal, not a result of this review: SRHD: primitive/conservative round trips, characteristic speeds, smooth waves, shock tubes, reflection, and transverse-velocity cases. Check EOS validity, rho and pressure positivity, and speeds below c. SRMHD: add relativistic Alfvén waves, magnetic shock tubes, and a rotor; specify the magnetic-divergence operator and every repair/floor. Fixed-metric GR: metric-aware flat-space limits, Michel/Bondi accretion, equilibrium stars, and torus configurations, with geometric source balance. Dynamical GR: couple a separately verified spacetime evolution; monitor Einstein constraints, baryon conservation, stellar oscillations, and waveform convergence before attempting mergers. Radiation or SRGSPH: keep each branch's state, boundary, conservation, transport closure, and reference tests explicit. Reuse the Newtonian examples as comparisons, not as evidence that a relativistic solver already exists. The historical conclusion is that progress comes from the combination of these layers. A new high-order reconstruction or a larger GPU run alone does not resolve primitive recovery, surface/atmosphere handling, constraint errors, or microphysical uncertainty.
