text.en: LEARNING RESOURCES公開コード・データ / Public code and data Textbooks: where to look next A working bookshelf for this atlas. Choose a book by the question you need to answer; this is a reading guide, not a ranking. Bibliographic years below identify the cited editions, not the invention dates of algorithms. The links lead to publisher records or author-maintained pages. We checked edition metadata and available descriptions or contents, not every derivation in every book. Chapter suggestions describe the atlas connection; they do not claim that all of a textbook has been implemented. A short starting path: Hirsch for the CFD framework; LeVeque for conservation laws and finite-volume reasoning; Toro for Riemann solvers; Patankar for pressure–velocity coupling; Saad for sparse iterative solves. Return to original papers when tracing a particular algorithm. Search the full reference library · All cataloged books · Download BibTeX Covers are supplied by Open Library for the listed ISBN. Each card links to Amazon Japan and the publisher or bibliographic record. The title stays visible when a cover is unavailable. CFD foundations and incompressible flow# Open Library record ISBN 9780750665940 Hirsch# Hirsch, Charles. Numerical Computation of Internal and External Flows: The Fundamentals of Computational Fluid Dynamics. Butterworth-Heinemann, 2007 · edition 2. Use this for the CFD framework: equations, grid properties, consistency, stability, discretization and solution procedures. The cited 2007 book is the second-edition fundamentals volume. Atlas connections: Differences, CFL, von Neumann analysis, and Lax · Structured, unstructured, and triangular meshes · Time integration and leapfrog. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ hirsch2007 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9783540530589 Fletcher / Volume I# Fletcher, Clive A. J. Computational Techniques for Fluid Dynamics 1: Fundamental and General Techniques. Springer, 1991 · edition 2. Use Volume I for PDE classification, weighted residual methods, steady and diffusion problems, and linear/nonlinear convection. It supplies the common numerical tools before the flow-specific algorithms of Volume II. Atlas connections: Differences, CFL, von Neumann analysis, and Lax · Continuous finite elements: from weak form to sparse assembly · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ fletcher1991v1 Open Library record ISBN 9783540536017 Fletcher / Volume II# Fletcher, Clive A. J. Computational Techniques for Fluid Dynamics 2: Specific Techniques for Different Flow Categories. Springer, 1991 · edition 2. Use Volume II to connect the general techniques of Volume I to different flow-equation categories and their computational solution procedures. Read assumptions and boundary conditions alongside each algorithm. Atlas connections: Incompressible flow: project with compatible discrete operators · Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution · Polar and cylindrical coordinates: tensors and viscosity. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ fletcher1991v2 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9783319996912 Ferziger · Perić · Street# Ferziger, Joel H.; Perić, Milovan; Street, Robert L. Computational Methods for Fluid Dynamics. Springer, 2020 · edition 4. Use this when connecting discrete operators to a practical CFD solution procedure, especially incompressible pressure–velocity coupling and boundary conditions. Atlas connections: Incompressible flow: project with compatible discrete operators · Polar and cylindrical coordinates: tensors and viscosity. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ ferziger2020 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780891165224 Patankar# Patankar, Suhas V. Numerical Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow. CRC Press (current publisher record), 1980. Use this for the physical logic of control-volume balances and SIMPLE-type pressure–velocity coupling. Keep the book exposition separate from the original algorithm papers. Atlas connections: Incompressible flow: project with compatible discrete operators · Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ patankar1980 Conservation laws, Riemann solvers and shocks# Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780521009249 LeVeque / finite volume# LeVeque, Randall J. Finite Volume Methods for Hyperbolic Problems. Cambridge University Press, 2002. Use this for weak solutions, finite-volume reasoning, wave propagation, limiters and multidimensional conservation laws. Companion Clawpack material connects the theory to computation. Atlas connections: Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM · Slope limiters: minmod, Superbee, MC, van Leer, and van Albada · Equation gallery: choose the equation before the algorithm. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ leveque2002 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9783540252023 Toro# Toro, Eleuterio F. Riemann Solvers and Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics: A Practical Introduction. Springer, 2009 · edition 3. Use this when deriving or comparing exact and approximate Euler Riemann solvers, contact waves and high-resolution shock-capturing methods. Atlas connections: Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution · Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM · Benchmark library. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ toro2009 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780387945293 Godlewski · Raviart# Godlewski, Edwige; Raviart, Pierre-Arnaud. Numerical Approximation of Hyperbolic Systems of Conservation Laws. Springer, 1996 · edition 1. Use this for a mathematical treatment of nonlinear hyperbolic systems and their numerical approximation, including Riemann problems and gas dynamics. Read it alongside LeVeque for finite-volume reasoning and Toro for solver construction. This entry cites the 1996 first edition; a revised second edition appeared in 2021. Atlas connections: Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution · Euler reconstruction: PPM, characteristics, WENO-Z and AUSM · A-stability, L-stability and error norms. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ godlewski1996book Finite differences and linear algebra# Open Library record ISBN 9780898716290 LeVeque / finite differences# LeVeque, Randall J. Finite Difference Methods for Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations: Steady-State and Time-Dependent Problems. SIAM, 2007. Use this for the consistency–stability–convergence chain, ordinary differential equations, boundary-value problems and finite-difference PDE solvers. Atlas connections: A-stability, L-stability and error norms · Time integration and leapfrog · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ leveque2007 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9781421407944 Golub · Van Loan# Golub, Gene H.; Van Loan, Charles F. Matrix Computations. Johns Hopkins University Press, 2013 · edition 4. Use this for conditioning, stable matrix factorizations, least squares and eigenproblems before choosing a solver solely by its name. Atlas connections: Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ golub2013 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780898715347 Saad# Saad, Yousef. Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems. SIAM, 2003 · edition 2. Use this for Krylov subspaces, GMRES, BiCG-family methods and preconditioners. The author provides the second-edition text and corrections. Atlas connections: Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ saad2003book Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780898713282 Barrett et al. / Templates# Barrett, Richard; Berry, Michael; Chan, Tony F.; Demmel, James; Donato, June; Dongarra, Jack; Eijkhout, Victor; Pozo, Roldan; Romine, Charles; van der Vorst, Henk. Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems: Building Blocks for Iterative Methods. SIAM, 1994. Use this open reference as a compact algorithm-and-selection companion for iterative linear solvers, with attention to matrix assumptions. Atlas connections: Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual · Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ templates1994 Multigrid: intuition, analysis and implementation# Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780898714623 Briggs · Henson · McCormick / A Multigrid Tutorial# Briggs, William L.; Henson, Van Emden; McCormick, Steve F. A Multigrid Tutorial. SIAM, 2000 · edition 2. Start here for why relaxation damps oscillatory error while coarse grids address the remaining smooth error. Follow the model problems into residual correction, restriction, prolongation and a working multigrid cycle. The second edition also introduces nonlinear problems and AMG. Atlas connections: Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration · Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ briggs2000book Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780127010700 Trottenberg · Oosterlee · Schüller / Multigrid# Trottenberg, Ulrich; Oosterlee, Cornelius W.; Schüller, Anton. Multigrid. Academic Press, 2001 · edition 1. Use this as the detailed reference after the tutorial: elementary multigrid theory, local Fourier analysis, smoother and coarse-grid choices, parallel implementation, systems and an AMG appendix. For the atlas Poisson comparison, use it to ask why a cycle converges and how its work changes; AMG, anisotropy and parallel performance need separate implementations and tests. Atlas connections: Diffusion, elliptic equations, boundary conditions, and iteration · Sparse and nonlinear systems: measure the actual residual · Particle gravity: PM, P³M, Tree, multipoles, and multigrid. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ trottenberg2001 Spectral bases and discontinuous Galerkin# Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780898714654 Trefethen# Trefethen, Lloyd N. Spectral Methods in MATLAB. SIAM, 2000. Use this for spectral differentiation, Fourier/Chebyshev examples and short reproducible programs. Supplement its limited barycentric-interpolation coverage. Atlas connections: Interactive experiment guide · Orthogonal polynomials and mesh basis functions. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ trefethen2000 Cover: Open Library ISBN 9780387720654 Hesthaven · Warburton# Hesthaven, Jan S.; Warburton, Tim. Nodal Discontinuous Galerkin Methods: Algorithms, Analysis, and Applications. Springer, 2008. Use this to connect nodal polynomial bases, quadrature and reference-element operators to DG interface fluxes and PDE algorithms. Atlas connections: Orthogonal polynomials and mesh basis functions · Interactive experiment guide. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ hesthaven2008book Time integration, geophysics and particles# Cover: Open Library ISBN 9783540306634 Hairer · Lubich · Wanner# Hairer, Ernst; Lubich, Christian; Wanner, Gerhard. Geometric Numerical Integration: Structure-Preserving Algorithms for Ordinary Differential Equations. Springer, 2006 · edition 2. Use this for symplectic maps, symmetric compositions, splitting and backward error analysis. Preserving symplectic structure does not mean exactly preserving the original Hamiltonian. Atlas connections: Symplectic integration: a canonical map, not an exact energy promise · Time integration and leapfrog. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ hairer2006book Cover: Open Library ISBN 9781441964113 Durran# Durran, Dale R. Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics: With Applications to Geophysics. Springer, 2010 · edition 2. Use this for dispersion, advection and time discretization in geophysical flows. Read it alongside the spherical-mesh and variable-staggering notes. Atlas connections: Spherical meshes and Arakawa A, B and C grids · Runge–Kutta families: stages, order, stability, and SSP. Amazon Japan ↗ Publisher / record ↗ Author / source ↗ durran2010 Open Library record ISBN 9780070291089 Hockney · Eastwood# Hockney, R. W.; Eastwood, J. W. Computer Simulation Using Particles. McGraw-Hill, 1981. Use this for particle–mesh thinking, force assignment and Fourier-based field calculations. The cited original year is 1981; the linked DOI is a later reissue. Atlas connections: Particle gravity: PM, P³M, Tree, multipoles, and multigrid · Gravity kernels: isolated FFTs and a periodic slab. Explicit solutions of Fisher’s equation for a special wave speed. Bulletin of Mathematical Biology 41, 835–840. An original article giving exact traveling waves at special speeds of Fisher’s equation. Distinguish these speeds from the general minimal propagation speed when testing reaction–diffusion profiles and fronts. This is a journal article, not a book. text.ja: MOLECULAR DYNAMICS / THERMOSTATS サーモスタット：温度制御と分布の比較 温度の平均だけでなく、揺らぎ・エルゴード性・時間相関を比べる。Nosé–Hoover、速度スケーリングから確率的・運動量保存型の手法まで。 12手法のうちLangevinとCSVRの2手法に専用実装。旧1自由度Langevin/BAOABの調和例を保持し、別版の同じOBABO分割で、非縮退2自由度の調和系とquartic係数λ=0.2の2自由度非調和系を比較します。CSVR単独の運動エネルギー核も検査。他の10手法は実装予定です。 JSON · Markdown 何の温度を制御するか 運動エネルギーをK、有効自由度数をfとすると、運動温度は T = 2 K / (f k_B)。拘束や重心運動の除去に応じてfを数え、流れがある場合は熱運動と平均流を区別する。回転自由度を含むかも明記する。 同じ平均温度でも分布は違う 古典的な二次形式の運動エネルギーを持つf個の独立な運動量自由度では、正準平衡で 2 K/(k_B T₀) は自由度fのχ²分布。平均Kはf k_B T₀/2、分散はf(k_B T₀)²/2となる。単純な速度スケーリング v ← √(T₀/T) v は適用直後のKを固定し、この揺らぎを再現しない。CSVRは確率的な係数で揺らぎを生成する別の手法である。 分布の標本化と運動の再現を分ける 正しい不変分布を持っていても、有限時間の軌道が十分に探索するとは限らない。また平衡分布が正しくても、摩擦や衝突で速度自己相関や拡散は変わり得る。有限時間刻みの誤差、熱浴の結合時間、乱数依存性まで含めて評価する。 CSVRとLangevin：正準分布・揺らぎ・相関を比べる 新しい比較は古典的な少自由度系に限定します。CSVRとLangevinに同じOBABO分割、自由度、温度、ポテンシャル、観測時刻を使い、分布・揺らぎ・相関を別々に評価します。従来のBAOAB調和振動子の結果は別の配布版として保持します。 CSVRの確率的更新と符号 CSVRは各運動量成分へ独立なノイズを加えず、全自由度の運動エネルギーを確率的に進め、同じ係数で運動量を拡大・縮小します。2007年論文の運動エネルギーSDEと厳密伝播式、2008年論文の符号付き係数を採用します。以下のhは熱浴のサブステップです。 同じ正規乱数RをKの更新と符号の判定に使います。少自由度では符号反転を捨てられません。Sは自由度f−1のχ²乱数で、f=1では厳密に0です。原著者は2007年論文のGammaによる二乗和生成の説明に誤植を指摘しているため、採用コードはχ²を直接生成します。 dK=Kˉ−Kτ dt+2KKˉfτ dW c=e−h/τ,a=(1−c)Kˉf,K+=(cK+a R)2+aS,R∼N(0,1),S∼χf−12 α=sign⁡ ⁣(cK+a R)K+/K,pi+=αpi 出典：Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · Algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling, author correction note 同じ分割順序で比べる 今回の2方式は、MD刻みをΔtとしてO(Δt/2)–B(Δt/2)–A(Δt)–B(Δt/2)–O(Δt/2)という同じOBABO順序を使います。Aは座標移動、Bは力による運動量更新、Oは熱浴です。CSVR更新式ではh=Δt/2を使います。OBABOの中央にはvelocity Verletがあり、両端の熱浴だけを入れ替えます。 τ=(2γ)⁻¹として、ポテンシャルのない熱浴の運動エネルギー緩和を揃えます。同じ数字のτを摩擦時間γ⁻¹と同一視しません。f=1では符号付きCSVRとLangevinの熱浴は同じ遷移分布となり、採用実装は与えたノイズを対応させて照合します。 以前のBAOAB例はB–A–O–A–Bという別の分割です。旧結果と独立線形参照は保存したまま、今回のOBABOの離散参照や誤差の結果に置き換えません。 τ=(2γ)−1,p+=e−γhp+mkBT0(1−e−2γh) Rphys(f=1) 出典：Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes 分布・揺らぎ・相関の三つの判定 静的な正準分布は両方式で共通です。運動量と運動エネルギー、瞬間温度の分布・平均・分散を確認し、位置の参照は調和系の解析分布、非調和系では別の数値求積から作ります。温度の平均だけが一致しても、揺らぎの再現は確認できません。 動的な相関は熱浴の方式と結合時間に依存します。座標q、運動量p、運動エネルギーK、全エネルギーHを観測し、方法間で一致することを成功条件にはしません。Langevinの調和系は連続行列指数とOBABOの離散定常共分散・伝播を分け、他の全系相関は測定値・不確かさ・刻み依存として示します。 ρK(t)=exp(−t/τ)という厳密参照は、Hamiltonianの力や位置更新を含まない熱浴単独の検査です。調和・非調和の全系ではKとUが交換するので、この式をそのまま当てません。 CDFの誤差は、入力で先に固定した位置・エネルギーの各5点、条件付き熱浴では3分位点などで調べた最大差です。分布全域の上限を取るKolmogorov–Smirnov統計量ではありません。全系の相関は正準参照の平均・分散で中心化・正規化しているため、有限刻みの零時差値が厳密に1とは限りません。 K=∑i=1fpi22mi,Kˉ=fkBT02,Tinst=2KfkB 2KkBT0∼χf2,Var⁡K=f(kBT0)22,Var⁡Tinst=2T02f CX(t)=⟨(X(t)−⟨X⟩)(X(0)−⟨X⟩)⟩,ρX(t)=CX(t)/CX(0) E[K+∣K]=cK+fa,Var⁡(K+∣K)=2fa2+4acK,ρK(t)=e−t/τ (bath only) 標本化の限界と実装の境界 正準な初期アンサンブルを保つ検査と、温度をずらした初期値から平衡へ近づく検査を区別します。複数の独立レプリカと固定seed、有限の観測窓を使い、標本誤差と刻み誤差・結合時間依存を混ぜません。採用した少自由度の検査は任意の初期値からの一般的な混合保証ではありません。 相関の標準誤差は、各時差で独立レプリカ間の積のばらつきから求めています。単一軌道の時間平均や、有効標本数を評価した誤差ではありません。非調和系の全系相関には独立な動的参照をまだ持たず、誤差ゼロとは表示しません。 全体を同じ係数でスケールする熱浴は、運動量空間の向きを直接ランダム化しません。対称性のある系で全運動量ゼロなどを保つ不変条件や、閉じた不変部分空間、同一周波数の特殊な系などによる探索不足を、正しいK分布だけで否定できません。今回の自由度には拘束や重心除去を追加していません。 正の熱浴刻みでK=0なら元の向きがなく、速度の比によるglobal rescaleは定義できないため、採用コードは明示的に拒否します。そこへ任意の向きを注入する別アルゴリズムとしては扱いません。非有限値、非正の温度・質量、無効な自由度や時間も検査します。 出典：Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling 採用式の一次資料と確認範囲 G. text.en: MOLECULAR DYNAMICS / THERMOSTATS Thermostats: temperature control and distributions Compare fluctuations, ergodicity and time correlations as well as mean temperature, from Nosé–Hoover and velocity rescaling to stochastic and momentum-conserving methods. Two of the 12 methods have dedicated implementations: Langevin and CSVR. Preserve the earlier one-degree-of-freedom harmonic Langevin/BAOAB case. A separate edition compares both baths with the same OBABO splitting for a nondegenerate two-degree harmonic system and a two-degree anharmonic system with quartic coefficient lambda=0.2, and checks the standalone CSVR kinetic-energy kernel. The other 10 methods remain planned. JSON · Markdown Define the controlled temperature With kinetic energy K and f active degrees of freedom, the kinetic temperature is T = 2 K / (f k_B). Count constraints and removed center-of-mass motion consistently, and separate thermal motion from streaming. State whether rotational degrees of freedom are included. Equal mean temperature does not imply equal distributions For f independent momentum degrees of freedom with classical quadratic kinetic energy, canonical equilibrium gives 2 K/(k_B T₀) a chi-square distribution with f degrees of freedom. Its mean K is f k_B T₀/2 and variance is f(k_B T₀)²/2. Direct rescaling v ← √(T₀/T) v fixes K immediately after application, removing these fluctuations. CSVR instead uses a stochastic factor to generate fluctuations. Separate sampling from dynamics An invariant distribution does not ensure adequate finite-time exploration. Even correct equilibrium sampling can coexist with friction- or collision-induced changes in velocity autocorrelations and diffusion. Assess integration error, heat-bath coupling time and random-seed dependence. CSVR and Langevin: shared canonical targets, distinct correlations The new comparison is limited to small classical systems. CSVR and Langevin use matched OBABO splitting, degrees of freedom, temperature, potential and observation times. Distribution, fluctuations and correlations are separate diagnostics. The earlier BAOAB harmonic results remain in their original release. The stochastic CSVR update and its sign CSVR evolves the total kinetic energy stochastically and scales all momenta together. The implementation uses the 2007 kinetic-energy SDE and exact propagator, with the signed factor in the 2008 paper. Here h denotes a thermostat substep. The same Gaussian R determines energy and sign. Momentum flips matter for a few degrees of freedom. Draw S directly from a chi-square law with f−1 degrees, with S=0 at f=1; this avoids the Gamma-construction typo identified by the original author. dK=Kˉ−Kτ dt+2KKˉfτ dW c=e−h/τ,a=(1−c)Kˉf,K+=(cK+a R)2+aS,R∼N(0,1),S∼χf−12 α=sign⁡ ⁣(cK+a R)K+/K,pi+=αpi Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling · Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · Algorithms: stochastic velocity rescaling, author correction note Compare with the same splitting Both new methods use O(Δt/2)–B(Δt/2)–A(Δt)–B(Δt/2)–O(Δt/2) for MD step Δt: A moves coordinates, B applies forces and O is the thermostat. The CSVR formula uses bath substep h=Δt/2. They share a velocity-Verlet core and differ in the bath updates. Set τ=(2γ)⁻¹ to match kinetic-energy relaxation for the force-free bath. This τ is not the friction time γ⁻¹. At f=1, signed CSVR has the Langevin transition law; a paired-noise check tests the implementation. The earlier BAOAB example uses a different B–A–O–A–B splitting. Its release and independent linear reference remain unchanged; the new OBABO references and errors do not replace them. τ=(2γ)−1,p+=e−γhp+mkBT0(1−e−2γh) Rphys(f=1) Sources: Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes Three separate questions: distribution, fluctuation and correlation Both methods share the static canonical target. Check momentum, kinetic energy and instantaneous-temperature distributions, means and variances. Position references are analytic for harmonic systems and use separate quadrature for the anharmonic case. Matching the mean temperature alone does not check fluctuations. Dynamic correlations depend on the method and coupling time. Measure position q, momentum p, kinetic energy K and total energy H without requiring agreement between methods. For harmonic Langevin, distinguish the continuous matrix exponential from the OBABO discrete stationary covariance/propagator. Other full-system correlations are measured with uncertainty and timestep dependence. The exact ρK(t)=exp(−t/τ) reference applies only to the isolated bath. Full harmonic or anharmonic motion exchanges K and U, so that expression is not used as its correlation target. CDF errors are maxima over predeclared checkpoints: five position/energy points and, for the conditional bath, three quantile points. They are not Kolmogorov–Smirnov suprema over the whole distribution. Full-system correlations use canonical-reference centering and normalization, so finite-step zero-lag values need not equal one exactly. K=∑i=1fpi22mi,Kˉ=fkBT02,Tinst=2KfkB 2KkBT0∼χf2,Var⁡K=f(kBT0)22,Var⁡Tinst=2T02f CX(t)=⟨(X(t)−⟨X⟩)(X(0)−⟨X⟩)⟩,ρX(t)=CX(t)/CX(0) E[K+∣K]=cK+fa,Var⁡(K+∣K)=2fa2+4acK,ρK(t)=e−t/τ (bath only) Sampling limits and implementation boundaries Preservation from a canonical initial ensemble and relaxation from temperature-perturbed starts are distinct checks. Use independent replicas, fixed seeds and finite observation windows; separate sampling uncertainty from timestep and coupling effects. These small tests do not guarantee mixing from arbitrary starts. Correlation standard errors use the spread of products across independent replicas at each lag; they are not uncertainties of a single-trajectory time average or an effective-sample-size estimate. No independent dynamical reference is claimed for the anharmonic full-system correlations, which are not presented as having zero error. A common scaling factor does not directly randomize momentum direction. A correct K distribution cannot rule out restricted sampling from invariant conditions such as zero total momentum in a symmetric system, or from invariant subspaces. The adopted degrees of freedom include no added constraints or removed center-of-mass mode. For a positive bath step, at K=0 the direction is undefined, so this implementation rejects global rescaling explicitly. It does not inject an arbitrary direction as an undocumented algorithm. Nonfinite or nonphysical parameters are also checked. Sources: Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling Primary sources for the adopted equations G. Bussi, D. Donadio and M. Parrinello (2007). Stochastic thermostats: comparison of local and global schemes · DOI: 10.1016/j.cpc.2008.01.006 Checked manuscript sections I–II, τ=(2γ)⁻¹, finite-step (8)–(9) and f=1; bibliography cross-checked with SISSA. Year denotes access, not the correction publication year. Runnable CSVR/Langevin validations Compare bath choices under the same OBABO splitting; separate step/coupling effects and independent-stream sampling uncertainty. Check distributions and temperature fluctuations separately from correlations. Langevin and CSVR correlations need not agree: they describe method-dependent sampling dynamics. Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt Distribution checks use a harmonic potential and fixed seeds. Exact position variance does not remove finite-step momentum bias. Evidence does not transfer to other thermostats, general molecules or long ab initio MD. Exact CSVR bath: conditional laws, fluctuations and kinetic correlation · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt A bath diagnostic, not another independent physical problem. Correct K sampling does not thermalize momentum directions by global scaling alone. The bath-only exp(−t/tau) identity is not a full-MD kinetic ACF. Statistical decisions apply to fixed seeds/budgets, not general mixing guarantees. CSVR versus Langevin: distributions, fluctuations and correlations of two harmonic modes · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt Global-CSVR and local-Langevin dynamical correlations are not required to agree. CDF errors are maxima over five declared points, not whole-line KS distances. Canonical-start preservation and the heated-start finite-time check do not prove ergodicity; tests retain an invariant unexcited-axis counterexample. No extrapolation to molecules, constraints or BOMD. Anharmonic CSVR versus Langevin: distribution checks against Boltzmann quadrature · ZIP · Stored results · Rerun receipt A small example for one separable two-mode quartic potential and fixed seeds. H is not treated as harmonic Gamma. No independent exact full-system dynamical reference is claimed, and neither matching correlations nor time order hidden by sampling noise is an acceptance claim. Molecular transport, quantum and ab initio MD are outside scope. Eight foundational entries Direct velocity rescaling Multiply velocities by a common factor to set the kinetic energy at each application. Simple deterministic rescaling does not reproduce canonical kinetic-energy fluctuations. A comparison case for distinguishing temperature control from canonical sampling. Ratio-based rescaling is undefined at T=0; the application interval also matters. Separate classical equilibrium fluctuation–dissipation settings from nonequilibrium approximations to nuclear quantum effects; neither is an electronic-structure solver. Other names: 一般化ランジュバン / colored-noise thermostat / 有色雑音 Method status, JSON and Markdown Ceriotti, Bussi & Parrinello (2009), Langevin Equation with Colored Noise for Constant-Temperature Molecular Dynamics Simulations LAMMPS: fix gle DPD pair thermostat Control temperature using dissipative and random pair forces. en.title: Particle leapfrog is a different formulation#

text.ja: 解説章公開コード・データ / Public code and data 英語原文が更新されています。この日本語訳は旧版に対応します。 時間積分とleapfrog法 空間再構成と時間積分は独立した選択です。空間離散化後、PDEはODE系dU/dt = L(U)になります。精度、安定性、単調性、散逸、計算量は両者に依存します。時間積分ノートではy′=i y、y(0)=1を使い、時間積分の選択を切り分けます。 ひとつの振動子と12手法# 厳密解exp(i t)は単位円をたどります。前進Eulerと後退Eulerは1次精度で、この無減衰振動子に対して前者は増幅、後者は減衰します。陽的RK2にはHeun／SSPRK(2,2)、陽的中点、Ralstonがあります。Kutta RK3、SSPRK(3,3)、SSPRK(4,3)は3次、古典的RK4とSSPRK(5,4)は4次です。陰的中点則は2次で、この線形振動子の振幅を保存しますが、位相には誤差があります。RK系譜の章と系譜ノートで段数・次数・SSP、非線形テストを比較できます。 y′=lambda yに対してz=lambda delta tと置くと、1ステップ増幅係数の例は、 RFE=1+z,RBE=11−z,Rmidpoint=1+z/21−z/2. です。このスカラー線形方程式では、3種のRK2、Kutta RK3／SSPRK(3,3)、古典的RK4のRK係数は、それぞれ2次、3次、4次までの指数関数のTaylor多項式になります。SSPRK(4,3)には4次項z⁴/48、SSPRK(5,4)には5次項もあります。同じスカラー増幅係数でも、非線形RK段階が同じとは限りません。SSP性は空間演算子の前進Euler限界に依存し、無条件安定ではありません。 leapfrog法には2つの根が必要# 1階の方程式系を中心差分で進める2ステップ漸化式は、 yn+1=yn−1+2zyn,ξ±=z±1+z2. です。zがゼロへ向かうと+1へ近づく根が物理モード、−1へ近づく根がステップごとに交互に変わる計算モードを担います。両方の根と重複度が重要です。z=i sigmaでは、|sigma|<1なら異なる2根の絶対値は1です。|sigma|=1では重根によって線形増大する解があり得るため、一般的な有界性の主張に端点を含めてはいけません。その上では一方の根が等比的に増幅します。 y(0)に加えて開始値が必要です。本実装ではRK4で1ステップ進め、必要に応じてy(1)へ実摂動epsilonを加えます。lambda=0なら、偶数番目の標本は1、奇数番目は1+epsilonとなり、計算モードを直接示せます。ノートの振動子では物理モードも同時に変化します。 Robert–Asselin系などの時間フィルターは、減衰と精度のトレードオフを伴って挙動を変えます。Williams（2009）を参照してください。初版にはフィルターを適用していません。 粒子leapfrogは別の定式化# 位置と速度をずらして更新するkick–drift法や、2階の力学系に対する速度Verletも、leapfrogと呼ばれることがあります。変数が異なる時刻位置にあり、シンプレクティックな解釈にはその構造を使います。上のスカラー漸化式は、完全なSPH粒子積分器の実演でも、一般の力学系の長時間エネルギー保存の証明でもありません。 ノートを再現して読む# from numart.time_integration import linear_trajectory, leapfrog_roots t, y = linear_trajectory(rate=1j, dt=0.1, steps=200, method='leapfrog') print(leapfrog_roots(0.1j)) ブラウザーでは、終了時刻20でPython計算した軌道から、12手法、7刻み幅、leapfrog開始摂動3種を選べます。不安定な標本では軸範囲が広がります。陰的求解とRK段数が異なるため、同じ時間区間でも同じ計算量とは限りません。テストでは時間収束次数、leapfrogの根、交互モード、中点則の振幅を確認します。 これらの振動子軌道はスカラー安定性係数を評価し、この線形テスト方程式ではRK段階と代数的に等価です。別の系譜ノートでは完全な非線形段階を評価します。空間安定性実験室、SPH、ALEへ進んでください。 正準的な力学写像# シンプレクティック積分の章では、調和・4次Hamilton系に対して、力学的なkick–drift–kick Verlet、吉田の4次合成、シンプレクティックEuler、陰的中点則を実装します。写像ノートではRK4と比較し、正準構造と厳密なエネルギー保存を分けます。 作用素分割の解説を追加しました。Lie–Trotterの1次合成とStrangの2次合成を、小さな厳密流の例で比較します。この章の既存ソルバーへ汎用分割実装を追加したという意味ではありません。 同じ反応拡散で両者を実行する軽量な固定入力例も追加しました。 作用素分割：Lie–Trotter と Strang の比較 歴史アトラス →計算結果のギャラリー →
text.en: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Time integration and leapfrog Spatial reconstruction and time integration are independent choices. After spatial discretization, a PDE becomes an ODE system dU/dt = L(U). Accuracy, stability, monotonicity, dissipation, and cost then depend on both parts. The time integration notebook isolates the temporal choice using y′ = i y, y(0) = 1. Twelve methods on one oscillator# The exact solution exp(i t) follows the unit circle. Forward Euler and backward Euler are first order: the former grows on this undamped oscillator, while the latter damps it. The explicit RK2 family includes Heun / SSPRK(2,2), explicit midpoint, and Ralston. Kutta RK3, SSPRK(3,3), and SSPRK(4,3) are third order; classical RK4 and SSPRK(5,4) are fourth order. Implicit midpoint is second order and preserves the amplitude of this linear oscillator. Its phase still has error. Read the RK family chapter and use the family notebook for stage/order/SSP comparisons and nonlinear tests. For y′ = lambda y, define z = lambda delta t. One-step amplification factors include RFE=1+z,RBE=11−z,Rmidpoint=1+z/21−z/2. The RK factors are the exponential Taylor polynomial through degree two, three, or four for the three RK2 variants, Kutta RK3 / SSPRK(3,3), or classical RK4 on this scalar linear equation. SSPRK(4,3) instead has a degree-four term z⁴/48; SSPRK(5,4) has an additional degree-five term. Shared scalar amplification does not make nonlinear RK stages identical. SSP properties depend on a forward-Euler bound for the spatial operator; they are not unconditional stability. Leapfrog needs two roots# The centered, two-step first-order-system recurrence is yn+1=yn−1+2zyn,ξ±=z±1+z2. The root tending to +1 as z tends to zero carries the physical mode; the root tending to −1 carries a computational mode alternating between steps. Both roots and their multiplicities matter. For z = i sigma, distinct roots have unit modulus when |sigma| < 1. At |sigma| = 1 the repeated root can give linearly growing solutions; do not include that endpoint in a general boundedness claim. Above it, one root grows geometrically. A starting value is required in addition to y(0). This implementation takes one RK4 step, optionally adding a real perturbation epsilon to y(1). At lambda = 0 that perturbation gives even samples equal to 1 and odd samples equal to 1+epsilon: a direct computational-mode demonstration. For the notebook’s oscillator it also perturbs the physical mode. Time filters such as the Robert–Asselin family modify this behavior, with their own damping and accuracy tradeoffs; see Williams (2009). No filter is applied in this edition. Particle leapfrog is a different formulation# A staggered kick–drift scheme for position and velocity, or velocity Verlet for a second-order mechanical system, is often also called leapfrog. Its variables live at different temporal locations and its symplectic interpretation uses that structure. The scalar recurrence above is not a demonstration of a complete SPH particle integrator or a proof of long-time energy conservation for general mechanics. Reproduce and read the notebook# from numart.time_integration import linear_trajectory, leapfrog_roots t, y = linear_trajectory(rate=1j, dt=0.1, steps=200, method='leapfrog') print(leapfrog_roots(0.1j)) The browser selects from Python-computed trajectories with fixed final time 20, twelve methods, seven step sizes, and three leapfrog starting perturbations. Axes expand for unstable samples. A matching time interval is not an equal-cost comparison: implicit solves and RK stages differ. Tests measure temporal refinement orders and check the leapfrog roots, alternating mode, and midpoint amplitude. These oscillator trajectories evaluate the scalar stability factor, which is algebraically equivalent to RK stages on this linear test equation; the separate family notebook evaluates full nonlinear stages. Continue with the spatial stability laboratory, SPH, and ALE. Canonical mechanical maps# The symplectic integration chapter now implements mechanical kick–drift–kick Verlet, a fourth-order Yoshida composition, symplectic Euler, and implicit midpoint on harmonic and quartic Hamiltonians. The map notebook compares them with RK4, separating canonical structure from exact energy conservation. An operator-splitting reading now compares first-order Lie–Trotter and second-order Strang with a small exact-flow illustration. It does not add a general splitting implementation to this chapter’s existing solver package. A lightweight fixed-input example now runs both on the same reaction–diffusion problem. Operator splitting: Lie–Trotter and Strang Historical atlas →Computed gallery →

text.en: Independent validation of nonlinear reaction–diffusion and pattern formation Follow a 1D periodic Schnakenberg system from finite-amplitude transients to post-growth patterns. Compare with a separate numerical reference and distinguish grid, time-step and reference errors. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs eleven NumPy/SciPy/pytest groups, comparing stored independent-library references with versioned, input-traced stored values. The existing common 22-case suite, including quantum convergence, remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts, criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-biology-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Finite-amplitude Schnakenberg transient: nonlinearity and independent reference Validate a finite-amplitude reaction-diffusion transient to t=8 with an independent Fourier–Galerkin reference, grid/time convergence and newly generated harmonics. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries 1D periodic x∈[0,2π), a=.1,b=.9,D=(.01,1). Common IC u=1+.08cos(2x)+.01cos(4x), v=.9−.03cos(2x)−.002cos(4x), restricted to a reflection-even, pi-periodic invariant subspace with a fixed origin. Editorial clarification Space refinement uses a separate Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference; time refinement uses an independently integrated Radau solution of the same FD semidiscrete system, not an exact continuous-PDE solution. Splitting error masked spatial error in the first coarse-step pilot. Steps were refined while keeping the acceptance criteria; the original input and failed metrics remain in the release. Adopted numerical method Strang-compose exact half-step diffusion of the FD matrix, diagonalized by FFT with symbol −4sin²(πk/N)/dx², and a full implicit-midpoint reaction step solved by local2×2 Newton iterations. FFT does not change FD space into spectral space. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics. note.ja: 空間も異なるcosine Fourier–Galerkin＋Radau参照（K32/64/96、cubic投影M=4(K+1)>4K、analytic Jacobian）とraw L1/L2/L∞を比較。参照のK感度とODE公差感度を別検査し、時間次数は同じFD半離散系を別実装Radauで積分した値に対して測定。平均L1・RMS L2・最大L∞を成分ごとに求め悪い方を採用。反応収支・全step正濃度・初期ゼロのk≥5（本対称性で最初はk6）・線形化との差を記録します。 収束ノルムと参照感度は固定最終時刻で判定し、途中スナップショット誤差は別の推移診断です。
note.en: Compare raw L1/L2/L∞ with a spatially independent cosine Fourier–Galerkin/Radau reference (K32/64/96, cubic projection M=4(K+1)>4K, analytic Jacobian). Separately check K and ODE-tolerance sensitivity. Measure time order against a separately implemented Radau integration of the SAME FD semidiscretization. Norms are per-species mean-absolute/RMS/maximum, then the worse species. Record source/sink balance, every-step positive concentrations, initially absent k≥5 (first allowed k6 here), and departure from linearization. Convergence norms and reference sensitivities are assessed at the fixed final time; intermediate snapshot errors are separate evolution diagnostics.

text.ja: Double Mach反射：多格子の軽量検証 既存のDouble Mach反射と同じ初期値・境界を使い、64×16・128×32・256×64の実2D Euler有限体積計算をT=.2まで実行します。別実装の有限格子参照との差、実際の境界流束収支、上部の入射衝撃位置と壁近傍を比較します。 共通22実行例の台帳とは別に管理する追加検証集です。配布ZIPを独立展開し、各グループの全固定入力と検査を実行した記録を示します。設定・手法・刻み幅の違いを独立した物理問題の数には加算しません。 通常の補助例CIはNumPy・SciPy・pytestで実行する11グループです。独立ライブラリ等の保存参照は版と入力を記録した保存値に照合します。量子収束を含む従来の共通22例は必要時の手動実行とし、既存の配布物・公差・履歴を保持します。 配布版を取得して実行する ZIPの atlas-double-mach-2026-11-23 フォルダで実行します。このコマンドは配布版の全1例を実行します。新規または空の出力先を指定してください。 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlibは保存図の任意の再描画にだけ使い、通常の科学計算には不要です。 Double Mach反射：多格子の軽量検証 既存のDouble Mach反射と同じ初期値・境界を使い、64×16・128×32・256×64の実2D Euler有限体積計算をT=.2まで実行します。別実装の有限格子参照との差、実際の境界流束収支、上部の入射衝撃位置と壁近傍を比較します。 手法・式・図・参照解 前提・単位・境界 無次元[0,4]×[0,1]、γ=1.4、Mach10。衝撃脚x=1/6、角度60度、後方状態(ρ,u,v,p)=(8,8.25√3/2,−4.125,116.5)、前方(1.4,0,0,1)。初期セルは衝撃のセル中心側で分類し、切断セルの厳密平均ではありません。左は後方流入、右はゼロ勾配、底はx<1/6で後方状態・他は滑り壁、上はx<1/6+(1+20t)/√3で後方状態を与えます。 編集上の補足 独立な有限格子の数値参照と比較する軽量例であり、2次元全場の厳密解ではありません。少数格子で測った衝撃位置・保存収支・wall jetの診断と、細い壁面噴流の収束を区別します。前向きステップは今回の実行対象に含めません。 採用した計算法 既存Numartの区分定数HLL流束と非分割x/y発散、Heun/SSPRK(2,2)を独立した小型配布物にし、両段の境界流束・状態確認を追加しました。CFL=.4を各方向の最大音響速度の和に適用し、上辺は各RK段の実時刻で更新します。状態floor、セル修復、隠れた刻み再試行はなく、不正段の生配列と履歴を残して失敗します。 ∂tU+∂xF(U)+∂yG(U)=0,U=(ρ,ρu,ρv,E)T xs(y,t)=16+y+20t3,γ=1.4,Ms=10 Δt=0.4[max⁡(∣u∣+c)/Δx+max⁡(∣v∣+c)/Δy]−1 ∑ij∣Cij∣(Uˉijn+1−Uˉijn)=Δt2(B(Un,tn)+B(U(1),tn+Δt)) 何と比較し、何を測るか 初回事前契約の20単体検査は合格。全3格子の実行前の読み取りレビューで、衝撃探索窓に前線が無い場合を拒否する診断ガードと1検査を追加し、旧契約・ソースを保持して改訂契約を固定しました。その21検査と全3計算・40判定が-W errorで合格しました。参照はRKDGキットで既に独立実行済みの、別実装primitive MUSCL/generalized-minmod θ=1.5/HLL/HeunのNy64/128データを再利用し、今回は参照PDEを再実行していません。Ny128保存量を保守的に制限して比較した密度L1は.08431/.05802/.03503、圧力L1は.09556/.06798/.04156。参照64/128増分は.00955/.01250で、最細主計算差の約.273/.301です。4保存量の境界収支の最大相対残差は約4.60e-13でした。 確認の限界と失敗条件 参照は有限格子の数値解で、厳密2D解でも独立のAthena/LAVA実行でもありません。HLLという流束族は共有しますが、参照は主計算の空間演算をimportしない別実装です。参照増分は不確かさの診断で誤差の上界ではありません。差には初期射影、動く境界の格子標本化、離散化と有限参照の影響が入り、傾きは厳密な空間次数や反射パターン全体の収束証明ではありません。上部前線の2セル差は物理幅では細分化で縮小しますが、セル単位の誤差は下がりません。壁近傍は固定領域x∈[1,2.75],y≤.25の比較で、ジェットを追跡した評価ではありません。最細でも領域最大uは主計算12.644に対し参照16.125で、薄いwall jet・巻き上がりは未解像です。前向きステップ、他の壁条件・一般摂動、高次精度、完全なパターン収束は今回の検証外です。 保存した実測値と判定 表示は丸めています。合否は固定入力の元の公差と丸め前の数値で判定し、全判定が合格した保存結果だけを表示します。 量 / metric実測値 n64 ny64 nx256 time0.2 steps811 density_l10.0350294425588 text.en: Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification Full 2D Euler finite volumes evolve the existing Double Mach initial/boundary data to T=.2 on64x16,128x32 and256x64 cells. Compare a separately written finite-grid reference, actual boundary-flux budgets, an upper incident-front position and a fixed near-wall region. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs eleven NumPy/SciPy/pytest groups, comparing stored independent-library references with versioned, input-traced stored values. The existing common 22-case suite, including quantum convergence, remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts, criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-double-mach-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Double Mach reflection: lightweight grid verification Full 2D Euler finite volumes evolve the existing Double Mach initial/boundary data to T=.2 on64x16,128x32 and256x64 cells. Compare a separately written finite-grid reference, actual boundary-flux budgets, an upper incident-front position and a fixed near-wall region. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Nondimensional[0,4]x[0,1], gamma1.4, Mach10. Shock footx=1/6, angle60degrees; postshock(rho,u,v,p)=(8,8.25sqrt(3)/2,-4.125,116.5), upstream(1.4,0,0,1). Initial cells are classified by their centers, not exact cut-cell means. Left postshock inflow, right zero-gradient, bottom postshock forx<1/6 and slip wall otherwise; top postshock forx<1/6+(1+20t)/sqrt(3). Editorial clarification A lightweight comparison with an independent finite-grid numerical reference, not an exact2D full-field solution. Separate measured shock location, conservation budgets and wall-jet diagnostics from convergence of the thin wall jet. Forward-facing step is outside this execution scope. Adopted numerical method The published Numart piecewise-constant HLL flux, unsplit x/y divergence and Heun/SSPRK(2,2) form a small standalone package with both-stage boundary accounting and state checks. CFL.4 uses the sum of directional maximum acoustic rates; the top boundary uses each actual RK stage time. No state floor, repair or hidden retry. Invalid stages retain raw arrays/history and fail. ∂tU+∂xF(U)+∂yG(U)=0,U=(ρ,ρu,ρv,E)T xs(y,t)=16+y+20t3,γ=1.4,Ms=10 Δt=0.4[max⁡(∣u∣+c)/Δx+max⁡(∣v∣+c)/Δy]−1 ∑ij∣Cij∣(Uˉijn+1−Uˉijn)=Δt2(B(Un,tn)+B(U(1),tn+Δt)) References and measured quantities The original preregistered20 unit tests passed. Before the full three-grid run, read-only review added an absent-front diagnostic guard and one test; the old contract/source are preserved and a revision contract was frozen. All21 tests, three final-time runs and40 gates passed with-W error. Previously independently executed Ny64/128 primitive MUSCL/generalized-minmod theta1.5/HLL/Heun data from the RKDG kit are reused; no reference PDE was rerun. Density L1 differences from conservatively restricted Ny128 are.08431/.05802/.03503 and pressure differences.09556/.06798/.04156. Reference64/128 increments are.00955/.01250, about.273/.301 of the finest primary differences. Maximum relative four-component boundary-budget residual is about4.60e-13. Verification limits and failures The reference is finite-grid numerical data, not an exact2D solution or an Athena/LAVA execution. The HLL family is shared, but reference spatial operators are separately written and not imported by the primary. The reference increment is an uncertainty diagnostic, not an error bound. Initial projection, sampled moving boundaries, discretization and finite-reference effects all enter the difference; the slope is no rigorous order or full reflection-pattern convergence proof. The upper-front discrepancy stays2cells while its physical width shrinks. Fixed near-wall ROIx in[1,2.75],y<=.25 is not feature tracking. Finest ROI maxu12.644 versus reference16.125 shows the thin wall jet/roll-up is unresolved. Forward step, other wall data, general perturbations, higher order and full-pattern convergence are unverified. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded. Acceptance uses original fixed-input tolerances and unrounded numbers; only stored results passing every check are presented. 量 / metricMeasured value n64 ny64 nx256 time0.2 steps811 text.ja: AMG・行列分解・固有値・求積 小規模な固定入力で、計算法・参照・誤差・収束・失敗条件を確かめます。 共通22実行例の台帳とは別に管理する追加検証集です。配布ZIPを独立展開し、各グループの全固定入力と検査を実行した記録を示します。設定・手法・刻み幅の違いを独立した物理問題の数には加算しません。 通常の補助例CIはNumPy・SciPy・pytestで実行する11グループです。独立ライブラリ等の保存参照は版と入力を記録した保存値に照合します。量子収束を含む従来の共通22例は必要時の手動実行とし、既存の配布物・公差・履歴を保持します。 配布版を取得して実行する ZIPの atlas-foundations-2026-11-22 フォルダで実行します。このコマンドは配布版の全4例を実行します。新規または空の出力先を指定してください。 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlibは保存図の任意の再描画にだけ使い、通常の科学計算には不要です。 行列から粗視化するAMG：残差と解誤差を分ける 正方形Poisson問題から得たSPD行列だけを階層構築へ渡し、平滑化集約AMGのV-cycleを実行します。7²・15²・31²未知数で独立疎行列直接解、解析的な離散正弦モード、連続解への2次収束を分けて検査します。 手法・式・図・参照解 前提・単位・境界 無次元の単位正方形、一定正係数の−Δu=f、全周同次Dirichlet境界、5点差分です。階層構築には座標・格子幅・nを渡さず、係数行列と暗黙の定数近似核だけを使います。入力は実対称正定値を前提とし、任意の不定値行列を扱うソルバーではありません。 採用した計算法 各行の最大非対角係数に対する相対強度からグラフを作り、貪欲な星型集約と余剰節点の隣接集約への付着で暫定補間Tを作ります。P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T、ω=4/(3ρ̄)、ρ̄はD⁻¹Aの絶対行和上界です。粗演算子はPᵀAP。前後2回のJacobi平滑化と最終小行列の直接解を用います。これは採用した小規模SA変種であり、原著の全構築法や収束定理の再現ではありません。 Ac=PTAP,P=(I−ωD−1A)T rk=b−Axk,ηk=∥rk∥2/∥b∥2 何と比較し、何を測るか 正規化残差、SciPy spsolveとの相対解差、連続正弦解への離散L²型誤差、観測次数、operator complexityを保存します。節点順を無作為に置き換えた行列も直接解と照合し、幾何学的な粗格子を暗黙に使っていないことを確認します。反復予算0は未収束と報告します。 確認の限界と失敗条件 3格子の固定スカラー問題だけの確認です。係数の大きな不連続、強い異方性、弾性系、任意の非構造格子、最適計算量・格子独立収束を保証しません。小さい残差だけを小さい解誤差の証明としません。 保存した実測値と判定 表示は丸めています。合否は固定入力の元の公差と丸め前の数値で判定し、全判定が合格した保存結果だけを表示します。 量 / metric実測値 前提・単位・境界 m≥nの小さな実行列が対象です。SVDの数値階数は最大特異値に対する相対しきい値10⁻¹²で定義し、零特異値方向を除くcompact因子を返します。QRは列ピボットなしで、階数判定には用いません。 採用した計算法 Householder反射を左から蓄積してRを上三角化し、Qを構成します。Jacobi SVDは列対の内積を小さくする直交回転を繰り返し、回転した列の長さを特異値とします。AᵀAを作って固有値を求める方法ではありません。最小二乗はQRの後退代入、階数落ちでは打切りSVDで求めます。 A=QR,QTQ=I A≃UrΣrVrT,xmin⁡=VrΣr−1UrTb 何と比較し、何を測るか QR/SVDの相対再構成誤差、Q/U/Vの直交性、SciPy LAPACK text.en: AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature Small fixed inputs connect numerical methods, references, errors, refinement and explicit failure conditions. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs eleven NumPy/SciPy/pytest groups, comparing stored independent-library references with versioned, input-traced stored values. The existing common 22-case suite, including quantum convergence, remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts, criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-foundations-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Matrix-based AMG: distinguish residual and solution error Build a smoothed-aggregation hierarchy from an SPD matrix alone and run V-cycles. Problems with 7², 15² and 31² unknowns distinguish independent sparse direct solutions, analytic discrete sine modes and second-order convergence to the continuum solution. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless unit square, constant-positive-coefficient −Δu=f, homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries and five-point differences. Hierarchy setup receives no coordinates, mesh width or n; it uses the coefficient matrix and an implicit constant near-null candidate. A real SPD input is assumed; arbitrary indefinite problems are outside scope. Adopted numerical method A graph based on row-relative off-diagonal strength supplies greedy star aggregates; leftover nodes attach to adjacent aggregates. Smooth tentative T via P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T with ω=4/(3ρ̄), where ρ̄ bounds the absolute row sums of D⁻¹A. Coarse operators are PᵀAP. V-cycles use two pre/post Jacobi sweeps and a terminal dense direct solve. This is a small adopted SA variant, not every construction or convergence theorem in the original paper. Ac=PTAP,P=(I−ωD−1A)T rk=b−Axk,ηk=∥rk∥2/∥b∥2 References and measured quantities Store normalized residuals, relative solution differences against SciPy spsolve, discrete-L²-type continuum errors, observed order and operator complexity. A randomly permuted matrix is also checked against a direct solution to expose hidden geometric ordering assumptions. A zero cycle budget reports nonconvergence. Verification limits and failures Only three fixed scalar grids are checked. Large coefficient jumps, strong anisotropy, elasticity, arbitrary unstructured meshes, optimal complexity and mesh-independent convergence are not certified. A small residual alone does not prove a small solution error. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Small real matrices with m≥n. Numerical rank uses a 10⁻¹² threshold relative to the largest singular value; compact factors omit null directions. QR has no column pivoting and is not used as a rank-revealing method. Adopted numerical method Householder reflectors triangularize R while accumulating Q. The SVD repeatedly rotates column pairs toward orthogonality and uses their resulting lengths as singular values; it does not diagonalize AᵀA. Least squares uses triangular back substitution for QR and truncated compact SVD for deficient rank. Singular-vector signs are not compared; zero matrices and budget exhaustion are tested. Verification limits and failures Not a full LAPACK replacement or validation of complex/wide matrices, arbitrary extreme scales or optimal relative singular-value accuracy. The 10⁻¹² cutoff defines numerical rather than exact mathematical rank. The experiment does not establish all hypotheses of the Demmel–Veselić accuracy results. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries The symmetric case is real symmetric; the nonsymmetric case is real with a known separated largest eigenvalue 5. Starting vectors use fixed seeds. Nonsymmetric Ritz values may be complex and are selected by largest real part. Adopted numerical method Lanczos uses its three-term recurrence plus two passes of full reorthogonalization; Arnoldi uses two-pass modified Gram–Schmidt. Nonsymmetric Ritz convergence is not assumed monotone. Tests include identity-matrix happy breakdown, zero-start rejection and insufficient dimension budgets. Verification limits and failures Unrestarted small-matrix educational examples with separated extreme eigenpairs. QR・SVD・最小二乗
Krylov固有値解法

この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: 各行の最大非対角係数に対する相対強度からグラフを作り、貪欲な星型集約と余剰節点の隣接集約への付着で暫定補間Tを作ります。P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T、ω=4/(3ρ̄)、ρ̄はD⁻¹Aの絶対行和上界です。粗演算子はPᵀAP。前後2回のJacobi平滑化と最終小行列の直接解を用います。これは採用した小規模SA変種であり、原著の全構築法や収束定理の再現ではありません。
note.en: A graph based on row-relative off-diagonal strength supplies greedy star aggregates; leftover nodes attach to adjacent aggregates. Smooth tentative T via P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T with ω=4/(3ρ̄), where ρ̄ bounds the absolute row sums of D⁻¹A. Coarse operators are PᵀAP. V-cycles use two pre/post Jacobi sweeps and a terminal dense direct solve. This is a small adopted SA variant, not every construction or convergence theorem in the original paper.

name.ja: この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: Householder反射を左から蓄積してRを上三角化し、Qを構成します。Jacobi SVDは列対の内積を小さくする直交回転を繰り返し、回転した列の長さを特異値とします。AᵀAを作って固有値を求める方法ではありません。最小二乗はQRの後退代入、階数落ちでは打切りSVDで求めます。
note.en: Householder reflectors triangularize R while accumulating Q. The SVD repeatedly rotates column pairs toward orthogonality and uses their resulting lengths as singular values; it does not diagonalize AᵀA. Least squares uses triangular back substitution for QR and truncated compact SVD for deficient rank.

name.ja: この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: Lanczosの3項漸化式に2回の全再直交化を加え、Arnoldiは修正Gram–Schmidtを2回行います。小さな射影行列T/HだけをNumPyのeigh/eigで解き、元空間へRitzベクトルを戻します。大きな元行列の密固有値計算は参照側だけで使います。
note.en: Lanczos uses its three-term recurrence plus two passes of full reorthogonalization; Arnoldi uses two-pass modified Gram–Schmidt. Only the small projected T/H is solved by NumPy eigh/eig before lifting Ritz vectors. A full dense solve of the original matrix is used only on the reference side.

name.ja: この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: Golub–Welschで対称Jacobi行列の固有値を節点、最初の固有ベクトル成分の平方の2倍を重みとします。適応Simpsonは区間を二分し、|S左+S右−S全|/15を局所推定として公差を配分します。評価回数と深さの上限を持ち、未達を成功としません。
note.en: Golub–Welsch obtains nodes from a symmetric Jacobi matrix and weights from twice the squared first eigenvector components. Adaptive Simpson bisects intervals and allocates tolerances using |Sleft+Sright−Swhole|/15 as a local estimate. Evaluation and depth limits report unmet targets explicitly.

note.ja: 独立NumPy/SciPy参照、行列再構成・直交性・特異値・階数・最小二乗残差を確認します。PDEの参照解カードとは別の線形代数検証です。 別版では条件数、右辺摂動、数値階数の閾値を変え、残差と係数の前進誤差を分けます。LAPACKと実際の二進入力から作る高精度参照の役割を区別し、QR／SVD全般や任意の悪条件行列の保証にはしません。
note.en: Check independent NumPy/SciPy references, reconstruction, orthogonality, singular values, rank and least-squares residuals. This is linear-algebra validation rather than a PDE reference-solution card. A separate release varies conditioning, right-hand-side perturbations and numerical-rank thresholds while separating residual from coefficient forward error. Distinguish LAPACK from high-precision references built from actual binary input; no general QR/SVD or arbitrary ill-conditioned-matrix guarantee is implied.

note.en: Check independent eigenvalue references together with Ritz/eigenpair residuals, orthogonality and iterative convergence. A separate release separates spectral spacing, nonnormality and Krylov dimension, distinguishing small residuals from true eigenvalue errors. A clustered-subspace comparison does not certify individual vectors or another physical model.

note.en: Use known polynomial integrals and independent quadrature references to check exactness, estimated errors and evaluation budgets. A separate release compares rule order, tolerance and cancellation sensitivity while distinguishing true integration error from the internal estimate. A missed narrow bump is an intended diagnostic; passing that diagnostic does not mean the integral estimate succeeded.

note.en: Original Lanczos and Arnoldi on symmetric/nonsymmetric 32×32 and 48×48 matrices measure convergence of the largest-real-part eigenpair over Krylov dimensions 4, 8 and 16, against independent full-matrix LAPACK references.

name.ja: Krylov固有値：クラスター部分空間と非正規感度
name.en: Krylov eigenvalues: cluster subspaces and nonnormal sensitivity

note.ja: 48次のクラスター固有値と強い非正規上三角行列で、次元4/8/16/32のLanczos・Arnoldiを測ります。残差・前進誤差・固有値条件数・不変部分空間を分けます。
note.en: Measure Lanczos and Arnoldi with dimensions4/8/16/32 on 48-dimensional clustered symmetric and strongly nonnormal triangular matrices. Distinguish residual, forward error, eigenvalue condition number and invariant subspace.

name.ja: Gauss–Legendreと適応求積：厳密次数・推定誤差・予算切れ
name.en: Gauss–Legendre and adaptive quadrature: exactness, error estimates and budgets

note.ja: Legendreの3項漸化式からGauss節点と重みを構成し、2n−1次までの多項式モーメントと指数関数を検査します。適応Simpsonは指数関数とLorentz型ピークを積分し、解析積分・独立QUADPACKと比較します。
note.en: Construct Gaussian nodes/weights from the Legendre recurrence and test polynomial moments through degree 2n−1 and an exponential. Adaptive Simpson integrates exponential and Lorentzian peaks, against analytic integrals and independent QUADPACK.

name.ja: 求積：狭いピーク・相殺・端点・誤差推定の盲点
name.en: Quadrature: narrow peaks, cancellation, endpoints and estimator blind spots

note.ja: Gauss次数と適応公差を走査し、狭いLorentzピーク、平方根端点、巨大な相殺、零積分、見逃すcompact bumpを解析積分とQUADPACKで検証します。
note.en: Vary Gauss order and adaptive tolerance on narrow Lorentz peaks, a square-root endpoint, severe cancellation, a zero integral and a deliberately missed compact bump, using analytic integrals and QUADPACK.

name.ja: 行列から粗視化するAMG：残差と解誤差を分ける
name.en: Matrix-based AMG: distinguish residual and solution error

note.ja: 正方形Poisson問題から得たSPD行列だけを階層構築へ渡し、平滑化集約AMGのV-cycleを実行します。7²・15²・31²未知数で独立疎行列直接解、解析的な離散正弦モード、連続解への2次収束を分けて検査します。
note.en: Build a smoothed-aggregation hierarchy from an SPD matrix alone and run V-cycles. Problems with 7², 15² and 31² unknowns distinguish independent sparse direct solutions, analytic discrete sine modes and second-order convergence to the continuum solution.

title.ja: 基盤手法：条件数・残差・収束と独立参照
title.en: Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references

text.en: Numerical foundations: conditioning, residuals, convergence and independent references Compare AMG, QR/SVD, Krylov eigenvalue methods and quadrature across fixed conditioning families. Separate residuals from forward error and matrix from integral conditioning; check independent references alongside convergence limits and diagnostic blind spots. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs eleven NumPy/SciPy/pytest groups, comparing stored independent-library references with versioned, input-traced stored values. The existing common 22-case suite, including quantum convergence, remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts, criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-foundations-conditioning-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. AMG: conditioning, anisotropy, residual and forward error Separate condition number from anisotropy on SPD systems of 49, 225 and 961 unknowns. Compare analytic spectra, independent sparse direct solutions and DST diagonalization, and measure how residual translates to forward error. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries A=T⊗I+εI⊗T with n=7/15/31 and ε=1/.1/.01. This is a known-solution algebraic diagnostic; continuum PDE validation remains in the earlier Poisson example. At fixed square n, κ₂ is independent of ε. Editorial clarification This diagnoses algebraic matrix conditioning and iteration error, separately from the earlier Poisson manufactured-solution PDE accuracy. Anisotropy and the 2-norm condition number need not vary together on a fixed grid. Distinguish residual, solution error and an exhausted iteration budget. Adopted numerical method Reuse the earlier MIT-licensed Atlas educational smoothed-aggregation AMG in a separate source release. Matrix-only hierarchy setup uses strength .08, Jacobi smoothing, fixed relative tolerance 10⁻¹⁰ and at most 180 V-cycles. Sine-transform spectral inversion is reference-side only. κ2(A)=cot⁡2 ⁣(π2(n+1)) ∥x−x^∥2∥x∥2≤κ2(A)∥b−Ax^∥2∥b∥2 References and measured quantities Store true residual, forward error, DST agreement, operator complexity and complete histories. Perturb a maximal-eigenmode RHS in the minimal-eigenmode direction and check the predicted relative amplification κ₂ with direct solves. Isotropic runs must converge; the predeclared anisotropy stress policy permits honestly reported budget exhaustion. A one-cycle control detects nonconvergence. Verification limits and failures Only a small constant-coefficient family is checked. Arbitrary coefficient jumps, unstructured grids, indefinite systems, optimal complexity and uniform convergence are outside scope. No claim that anisotropy necessarily increases κ₂ or monotonically worsens convergence. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded. Acceptance uses original fixed-input tolerances and unrounded numbers; only stored results passing every check are presented. 量 / metricMeasured value maximum_condition_2414.345062232 name.ja: 代数的マルチグリッド（AMG）
QR・SVD・最小二乗
Krylov固有値解法
Gauss求積・適応積分
この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: MITライセンスの既存アトラス教材の平滑化集約AMGを新しい独立ソースへ再利用します。階層は行列だけから構築し、強度閾値.08、Jacobi平滑化、固定相対公差10⁻¹⁰、最大180 V-cycleを使います。DSTの正弦変換による直接反転は参照側だけです。
note.en: Reuse the earlier MIT-licensed Atlas educational smoothed-aggregation AMG in a separate source release. Matrix-only hierarchy setup uses strength .08, Jacobi smoothing, fixed relative tolerance 10⁻¹⁰ and at most 180 V-cycles. Sine-transform spectral inversion is reference-side only.

name.ja: この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: Householder QR、片側Jacobi SVD、三角後退代入を実装します。SVDの数値階数閾値を10⁻⁸/10⁻¹²/10⁻¹⁴へ変え、同じ切捨て規約のLAPACK解と比較します。正規方程式の計算例は追加していません。
note.en: Implement Householder QR, one-sided Jacobi SVD and triangular back substitution. Vary rank cutoffs 10⁻⁸/10⁻¹²/10⁻¹⁴ and compare with LAPACK solutions using the same truncation convention. No executed normal-equations comparison is added.

name.ja: この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: 全再直交化Lanczosと2回MGSのArnoldiで縮約し、小さい射影行列だけを密に解きます。上位2ベクトルはQRで張る空間へ変換し、符号や回転に不変な射影行列差を測ります。
note.en: Use fully reorthogonalized Lanczos and two-pass MGS Arnoldi; only the small projected matrix is solved densely. Compare QR-spanned top-two subspace projectors, invariant under signs and cluster rotations.

name.ja: この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: Golub–Welschの節点・重みと、局所差/15を用いる適応Simpsonを実装します。端点ではx=t²変換を別対照とし、狭いbumpには既知支持区間を分割した対照を用意します。これは一般的な自動救済機構ではありません。
note.en: Implement Golub–Welsch nodes/weights and adaptive Simpson with a local difference/15 estimate. Companion checks use x=t² for the endpoint and a known-support split for the narrow bump; these are not general automatic rescue mechanisms.

name.ja: AMGの条件数・異方性・残差と前進誤差：参照・検証
name.en: AMG: conditioning, anisotropy, residual and forward error — references and checks

note.ja: 真の残差、独立直接解との差、DSTとの差、operator complexity、全残差履歴を保存します。最大固有値方向の右辺へ最小固有値方向の摂動を加え、相対増幅κ₂を直接解で照合します。等方例は収束必須、異方性stress例は予算終了も正直に記録する事前基準です。1-cycle対照は未収束を検出します。
note.en: Store true residual, forward error, DST agreement, operator complexity and complete histories. Perturb a maximal-eigenmode RHS in the minimal-eigenmode direction and check the predicted relative amplification κ₂ with direct solves. Isotropic runs must converge; the predeclared anisotropy stress policy permits honestly reported budget exhaustion. A one-cycle control detects nonconvergence.

name.ja: QR/SVD：既定特異値・摂動増幅・数値階数：参照・検証
name.en: QR/SVD: prescribed spectra, perturbation gain and numerical rank — references and checks

note.ja: 再構成・直交性・特異値・右辺摂動による解差・最小二乗停留残差・厳密階数2の対照を保存します。高精度参照は実二進入力を整数比へ変換し、mpmath 1.3.0のSVDとQRを独立実行済みです。SHAと全4入力・両精度の完全性を実行時に検査し、不一致を解析解へ置換しません。
note.en: Save reconstruction, orthogonality, singular values, solution perturbations, least-squares stationarity and an exact rank-two control. The mpmath1.3.0 SVD and QR reference was actually executed using integer-ratio conversions of binary inputs. Runtime SHA and completeness guards check all four inputs at both precisions and never substitute analytic truth after a mismatch.

name.ja: Krylov固有値：クラスター部分空間と非正規感度：参照・検証
name.en: Krylov eigenvalues: cluster subspaces and nonnormal sensitivity — references and checks

note.ja: 解析的対角固有値とSciPy密固有値、左右固有ベクトルによる条件数を照合します。別に構成した2×2擬固有対ではK=1000で残差約2.5×10⁻⁸に対し固有値誤差.005を示します。これは反復法が出力した失敗例ではなく、残差だけでは保証できないことを示す感度対照です。
note.en: Compare analytic triangular eigenvalues, SciPy dense eigenvalues and left/right eigenvector condition numbers. A separately constructed2×2 pseudoeigenpair has residual about2.5×10⁻⁸ but eigenvalue error.005 at K=1000. It is a sensitivity control, not a failure produced by the iterative solver.

name.ja: 求積：狭いピーク・相殺・端点・誤差推定の盲点：参照・検証
name.en: Quadrature: narrow peaks, cancellation, endpoints and estimator blind spots — references and checks

note.ja: roots_legendre、解析atan積分、2/3、bumpの256w/315、独立QUADPACKを比較します。QUADPACKの状態・推定誤差・評価回数・警告文も保存します。相殺はε_machine×積分絶対量に対応する絶対予算を使います。初期5点が全て零のbumpでは推定誤差0と実誤差約.00813を明示します。
note.en: Compare roots_legendre, analytic atan integrals,2/3,the bump integral256w/315 and independent QUADPACK. Preserve QUADPACK status, estimated error, evaluation count and warning message. Cancellation uses a roundoff-aware absolute budget. When all initial five bump samples vanish, expose estimated error0 versus actual error about.00813.

name.ja: AMGの条件数・異方性・残差と前進誤差
name.en: AMG: conditioning, anisotropy, residual and forward error

note.ja: 49・225・961未知数のSPD行列で、条件数と異方性を別々に変えます。解析スペクトル、独立疎行列直接解、DST対角化を比較し、同じ残差でも解誤差が条件数に依存することを確かめます。
note.en: Separate condition number from anisotropy on SPD systems of 49, 225 and 961 unknowns. Compare analytic spectra, independent sparse direct solutions and DST diagonalization, and measure how residual translates to forward error.

name.ja: QR/SVD：既定特異値・摂動増幅・数値階数
name.en: QR/SVD: prescribed spectra, perturbation gain and numerical rank

note.ja: 二進で厳密に表現できる16×4行列の条件数を1から2³⁶まで変え、再構成誤差と解誤差を分けます。実際のbinary64入力に対し別環境で実行した80/120桁参照とLAPACKを比較します。
note.en: Vary condition number from 1 to 2³⁶ for exactly representable 16×4 dyadic matrices, separating reconstruction from forward solution error. Compare LAPACK and separately executed 80/120-digit references for the actual binary64 inputs.

name.ja: Krylov固有値：クラスター部分空間と非正規感度
name.en: Krylov eigenvalues: cluster subspaces and nonnormal sensitivity

note.ja: 48次のクラスター固有値と強い非正規上三角行列で、次元4/8/16/32のLanczos・Arnoldiを測ります。残差・前進誤差・固有値条件数・不変部分空間を分けます。
note.en: Measure Lanczos and Arnoldi with dimensions4/8/16/32 on 48-dimensional clustered symmetric and strongly nonnormal triangular matrices. Distinguish residual, forward error, eigenvalue condition number and invariant subspace.

name.ja: 求積：狭いピーク・相殺・端点・誤差推定の盲点
name.en: Quadrature: narrow peaks, cancellation, endpoints and estimator blind spots

note.ja: Gauss次数と適応公差を走査し、狭いLorentzピーク、平方根端点、巨大な相殺、零積分、見逃すcompact bumpを解析積分とQUADPACKで検証します。
note.en: Vary Gauss order and adaptive tolerance on narrow Lorentz peaks, a square-root endpoint, severe cancellation, a zero integral and a deliberately missed compact bump, using analytic integrals and QUADPACK.

text.ja: 多峰性MCMC：混合不良と収束診断の独立検証 二峰性分布で、局所的な閉じ込めと峰間の移動を比べます。自己相関・有効標本数・収束診断の計算を独立実装と照合し、診断値だけでは見逃す探索不足も示します。 共通22実行例の台帳とは別に管理する追加検証集です。配布ZIPを独立展開し、各グループの全固定入力と検査を実行した記録を示します。設定・手法・刻み幅の違いを独立した物理問題の数には加算しません。 通常の補助例CIはNumPy・SciPy・pytestで実行する11グループです。独立ライブラリ等の保存参照は版と入力を記録した保存値に照合します。量子収束を含む従来の共通22例は必要時の手動実行とし、既存の配布物・公差・履歴を保持します。 配布版を取得して実行する ZIPの atlas-mcmc-2026-11-22 フォルダで実行します。このコマンドは配布版の全2例を実行します。新規または空の出力先を指定してください。 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlibは保存図の任意の再描画にだけ使い、通常の科学計算には不要です。 多峰性MCMC：峰への閉じ込め・偽の安心・大域提案 同じ2峰密度を、分散初期値の局所MH・同じ峰からの局所MH・対称reflectionを混ぜるMHで比較。期待した混合不良の検出と、実際の峰間移動を分けて検証します。 手法・式・図・参照解 前提・単位・境界 無次元1D標的p=.5N(−6,1)+.5N(6,1)、平均0/分散37/正側占有.5。3固定seed・4鎖、burn1024、保持16384標本/鎖。prefix1024/4096/16384は入れ子で独立再試行ではありません。棄却と自己遷移を保持します。 編集上の補足 この検証の「合格」は、混合する系列の分布確認と、意図的に混合しない系列の失敗・診断の盲点を正しく示したことを表します。全系列が収束したという意味ではありません。RhatやESSは観測量・有限標本・初期値に依存し、同じ峰に閉じ込められた全鎖では良く見えることがあります。反射ジャンプは既知の対称性を利用する比較用の提案であり、一般の未知の多峰性を解く保証ではありません。 採用した計算法 ESS、鎖内だけのACF/ESSを記録。分散trapped鎖はpooled分布が良くてもRhat/多鎖ESSで失敗、same-mode鎖はRhatが良くても既知標的に失敗する対照です。scenario passはこの期待失敗を検出できた意味です。CDF差は指定点最大でKS全域距離・IID検定p値ではありません。 確認の限界と失敗条件 固定seed・有限予算の教育用実験です。局所Gaussian text.en: Multimodal MCMC: independent checks of poor mixing and convergence diagnostics Compare local trapping and between-mode movement on a bimodal target. Check autocorrelation, effective sample size and convergence diagnostics against an independent implementation, and expose missed exploration that diagnostics alone cannot detect. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs eleven NumPy/SciPy/pytest groups, comparing stored independent-library references with versioned, input-traced stored values. The existing common 22-case suite, including quantum convergence, remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts, criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-mcmc-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Multimodal MCMC: trapping, false reassurance and a global proposal Compare dispersed local MH, same-mode local MH and symmetry-informed reflection/local MH on the same bimodal target. Separate detecting expected mixing failures from successful finite-budget mode exploration. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless1D target p=.5N(−6,1)+.5N(6,1), mean0/variance37/positive occupancy.5. Three fixed seeds, four chains,1024 warmup and16384 retained draws/chain. Prefixes1024/4096/16384 are nested, not independent replications. Rejections/self-transitions are retained. Editorial clarification Passing this validation means confirming the well-mixing run and correctly exposing failures and diagnostic blind spots in deliberately trapped runs; it does not mean every run converged. Rhat and ESS depend on the observable, finite sample and initial states, and can look reassuring when all chains miss the same mode. Reflection jumps exploit known target symmetry for this comparison and do not guarantee exploration of arbitrary unknown multimodal targets. Adopted numerical method Local scale.8; mixed uses y=−x+.8Z with probability.1, otherwise y=x+.8Z. The state-independent mixture is symmetric q(y|x)=q(x|y), so MH uses the log-target ratio. Chains use independent PCG64 streams, with no adaptation or removal of rejected states. π(x)=12ϕ(x+6)+12ϕ(x−6),E[X]=0,Var⁡X=37 F(x)=12Φ(x+6)+12Φ(x−6),P(X>0)=12 q(y∣x)=(1−p)ϕs(y−x)+pϕs(y+x)=q(x∣y),s=.8, p=.1 α(x,y)=min⁡{1,π(y)/π(x)},In=1{Xn>0} References and measured quantities Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value. Verification limits and failures An educational fixed-seed, finite-budget experiment. The local Gaussian RW is theoretically irreducible MH; finite-time trapping is not called a nonergodic algorithm. Small Rhat, large ESS and pooled-CDF agreement cannot rule out undiscovered modes. Symmetry-informed reflection is not a generic multimodal solver. No quantum calculations. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded. note.ja: 局所幅.8、mixedのみ確率.1でy=−x+.8Z、それ以外y=x+.8Z。混合率は状態非依存でq(y|x)=q(x|y)のため対数標的比でMH判定。各鎖は独立PCG64 stream、提案の適応・棄却の間引きなし。
note.en: Local scale.8; mixed uses y=−x+.8Z with probability.1, otherwise y=x+.8Z. The state-independent mixture is symmetric q(y|x)=q(x|y), so MH uses the log-target ratio. Chains use independent PCG64 streams, with no adaptation or removal of rejected states.

name.ja: この実行例の式と条件

note.ja: 原著式から独自実装。odd長は中央1標本を落としてsplit、平均順位のBlom式は訂正済みS+1/4、fold後再rank、最大Rhatを採用。bulk ESSはrank split、tail ESSは元の全鎖のType7分位点を先に求めた≤indicatorをsplit。Geyer initial-positive/monotoneと宣言した端点処理・tau≥1/log10(total)を用い、反相関ESSをNへclipしません。
note.en: Original equation-based implementation: split with the odd center dropped, average-tie Blom ranks using corrected S+1/4, re-rank folded deviations, and take the larger Rhat. Bulk ESS uses rank-split draws; tail ESS first determines Type7 quantiles on original full draws, then splits <= indicators. Use initial-positive/monotone pairs, declared endpoint handling and tau>=1/log10(total), without clipping antithetic ESS to N.

note.ja: 既知の2峰Gaussian混合の解析的な密度・モーメント・指定点CDF・正側占有と照合し、診断量は独立ArviZ参照で確認します。峰への閉じ込めと多鎖診断の限界を区別し、局所診断の良さを全体混合の保証にしません。
note.en: Compare with the known bimodal Gaussian mixture’s analytic density, moments, declared CDF points and positive occupancy, and check diagnostics against independent ArviZ references. Distinguish trapping from diagnostic limitations; reassuring local diagnostics do not guarantee global mixing.

name.ja: 多峰性MCMC：峰への閉じ込め・偽の安心・大域提案：参照・検証
name.en: Multimodal MCMC: trapping, false reassurance and a global proposal — references and checks

note.ja: 解析平均・分散・CDFの指定7点・正側占有と照合。各鎖の占有率と峰間遷移、rank/folded split Rhat、bulk/tail/mean・modeindicator ESS、鎖内だけのACF/ESSを記録。分散trapped鎖はpooled分布が良くてもRhat/多鎖ESSで失敗、same-mode鎖はRhatが良くても既知標的に失敗する対照です。scenario passはこの期待失敗を検出できた意味です。CDF差は指定点最大でKS全域距離・IID検定p値ではありません。
note.en: Compare with analytic moments, seven declared CDF points and positive occupancy. Record per-chain occupancies/transitions, rank/folded split Rhat, bulk/tail/mean and mode-indicator ESS, and within-only ACF/ESS. Dispersed trapped chains can have a good pooled distribution yet fail between-chain diagnostics; same-mode chains can have reassuring Rhat yet fail the known target. A control scenario passes when its intended failure is detected. CDF error is a declared-point maximum, not whole-line KS distance or an IID-test p-value.

note.ja: 実鎖9組×3prefix×x/indicator＋8小fixtureの62組。同じbytesを再生成して照合し、通常の有限値Rhat/ESS/ACFと、定数・鎖内ゼロ分散・odd・ties・shift・scaleを検査。別の直接lag和、定常AR(1)の無限列tau=(1+rho)/(1−rho)で有限推定の誤差も測定します。routineは保存参照との照合で、ArviZのその場再実行は任意の別手順です。
note.en: 62 datasets: nine actual chains times three prefixes times x/indicator plus eight small fixtures. Regenerate and hash identical bytes; compare ordinary finite Rhat/ESS/ACF and test constants, zero within-chain variance, odd lengths, ties, shift and scale. Direct lag sums and infinite-series stationary-AR(1) tau=(1+rho)/(1−rho) provide separate checks of finite estimates. Routine runs compare stored references; live ArviZ regeneration is a separate optional procedure.

text.ja: 流体・MHDの独立照合とCT／GLM 小規模な固定入力で、計算法・参照・誤差・収束・失敗条件を確かめます。 共通22実行例の台帳とは別に管理する追加検証集です。配布ZIPを独立展開し、各グループの全固定入力と検査を実行した記録を示します。設定・手法・刻み幅の違いを独立した物理問題の数には加算しません。 通常の補助例CIはNumPy・SciPy・pytestで実行する11グループです。独立ライブラリ等の保存参照は版と入力を記録した保存値に照合します。量子収束を含む従来の共通22例は必要時の手動実行とし、既存の配布物・公差・履歴を保持します。 配布版を取得して実行する ZIPの atlas-mhd-2026-11-22 text.en: Independent fluid/MHD comparisons and CT/GLM Small fixed inputs connect numerical methods, references, errors, refinement and explicit failure conditions. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs eleven NumPy/SciPy/pytest groups, comparing stored independent-library references with versioned, input-traced stored values. The existing common 22-case suite, including quantum convergence, remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts, criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-mhd-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Orszag–Tang: CT, GLM and independent Athena++ Compare CT and GLM density, magnetic field, conservation and div B for the same periodic Orszag–Tang data, against separately executed Athena++. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Unit square, gamma=5/3, mu0=1, vz=Bz=0, t=0.05. rho=25/(36pi), p=5/(12pi), v=(-sin2piy,sin2pix), B=(-sin2piy,sin4pix)/sqrt(4pi). Editorial clarification The adopted GLM uses ch=3 and damping rate kappa=0.18 ch n, with n cells per axis: damping is grid dependent. Both use the same continuous initial field, final time and CFL, while actual step counts and native div B operators differ. Adopted numerical method Reuse the published first-order Rusanov/forward-Euler solvers: shared corner-EMF discrete curl for CT and cell-centered hyperbolic/parabolic GLM cleaning. Independent Athena++ uses HLLD, PLM and RK2. ∇⋅B=0,Bt+∇×E=0 References and measured quantities Measure density/By L1 error, mass/energy drift and positivity on 16²/32²/64². Check the independent 128²/256² reference and conservatively restrict its fine-cell averages. Verification limits and failures Face CT divergence and centered GLM divergence use different operators; common cell-centered diagnostics are also reported. Athena initializes face-averaged magnetic fields by differencing a vector potential, so comparison includes discretization differences of identical continuous data. This is a short planar test, not validation of shocks, 3D, UCT or CTU. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded. text.ja: CTとGLM：同条件の独立照合・格子・時間収束 数値流束族・LLF係数・時間刻み・物理減衰率を固定し、CTとGLMの離散化を比較します。構成した滑らかな厳密解と独立Athena++参照を使い、格子誤差・時間積分誤差・参照自身の差を分けて確かめます。 共通22実行例の台帳とは別に管理する追加検証集です。配布ZIPを独立展開し、各グループの全固定入力と検査を実行した記録を示します。設定・手法・刻み幅の違いを独立した物理問題の数には加算しません。 通常の補助例CIはNumPy・SciPy・pytestで実行する11グループです。独立ライブラリ等の保存参照は版と入力を記録した保存値に照合します。量子収束を含む従来の共通22例は必要時の手動実行とし、既存の配布物・公差・履歴を保持します。 配布版を取得して実行する ZIPの atlas-mhd-convergence-2026-11-22 フォルダで実行します。このコマンドは配布版の全3例を実行します。新規または空の出力先を指定してください。 python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlibは保存図の任意の再描画にだけ使い、通常の科学計算には不要です。 CT・GLM：移動する磁気静力学平衡の格子・時間収束 非零の磁気力と圧力勾配が釣り合う構成厳密解を使い、同じ初期セル状態・流束の速度上界・刻み列でCT/GLMを比較します。 手法・式・図・参照解 入力・検証手順の履歴 · 初回の入力 前提・単位・境界 周期単位正方形、γ=5/3、μ₀=1、平面MHD。A=.05[cos2π(x−.3t)+cos2π(y−.2t)]、B=(Ay,−Ax)、ρ=1、v=(.3,.2)、p=.1+(2π)²A²/2、t=.1。保存変数の解析的セル平均を比較します。公刊の標準問題名を借りない構成検証例です。 編集上の補足 この滑らかな移流平衡はアトラスで構成した厳密解です。保存量のセル平均を比較し、そのセル平均から回復する圧力と圧力自体の厳密なセル平均を区別します。同じ半離散空間演算子に別の時間積分を適用した参照は、時間誤差の照合であり独立PDEソルバーとは呼びません。 採用した計算法 両法とも区分定数・同じ固定Rusanov速度α=3・前進Eulerです。CTは面Bと共有算術corner EMF、GLMはcell B/ψとch=3・物理減衰率κ=2を使用。全格子で同じ384刻み、両法のdt列も同一です。CT面平均から復元した初期cell BとGLM初期Bが一致します。 A=a[cos⁡k(x−ut)+cos⁡k(y−vt)],B=(Ay,−Ax),Jz=−ΔA=k2A p=p0+12k2A2,∇p=Jz∇A=J×B Uˉij=1ΔxΔy∫KijU dx dy,p(Uˉ)≠pˉ Um+1=Um+Δt Lh(Um),Csum=αΔt(Δx−1+Δy−1) 何と比較し、何を測るか 16²/32²/64²の保存変数L1/L2/L∞誤差と観測次数を測ります。最細格子の刻み倍増差を空間誤差の.1以下と比較。時間収束は固定8²で16/32/64/128刻みを、許容誤差・最大刻みを二重に細分したDOP853へ照合します。質量・E、正値性、native CT divと共通cell div、ψも記録します。 確認の限界と失敗条件 定数LLF粘性・周期中心演算子では、GLMのdiv=ψ=0部分空間は丸めまで保たれます。本例は結合MHDの精度を調べ、能動的cleaningは別の非物理診断対照で調べます。p(q平均)はpの厳密平均と同一ではありません。DOP853は時間だけ独立で空間RHSは共有します。刻み倍増差は経験的汚染目安で厳密誤差上界ではなく、CT/GLMの内部表現差を含む有限離散化全体の比較です。
